## P2 - `netem` on `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoints silently impairs root-namespace interfaces via the veth-stitch path

**Location:** [links/link&#95;veth&#95;stitched.go:34-69](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth_stitched.go#L34-L69)

**Problem:** `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` rejects `netem` on `host`/`mgmt-net` endpoints &#40;[`links/link_veth.go:71-73`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth.go#L71-L73)&#41;, but the early return to veth-stitch at [`links/link_veth.go:58-60`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth.go#L58-L60) bypasses that check, and `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve`/`buildVEthStitchSegment` perform no `netem` validation while `EndpointRaw.Resolve` attaches the `netem` unconditionally for every node kind. `LinkVEthStitched.GetEndpoints()` returns the node-side endpoints, so `applyLinkImpairments` applies the impairment via `GenericLinkNode.ExecFunction`, which executes in the root namespace.

**Trigger:** A brief link with an `host:` or `mgmt-net:` endpoint carrying `netem` together with an SR-SIM endpoint &#40;`sros.DefaultLinkType()` returns `LinkTypeVethStitch`, [`nodes/sros/sros.go:1892-1894`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/nodes/sros/sros.go#L1892-L1894)&#41;, or a long-form `type: veth-stitch` link with a `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoint carrying `netem`.

**Impact:** A `netem` qdisc is silently installed on the lab `host`&#39;s real interface &#40;or the management bridge port&#41; in the root namespace, degrading `host` networking with `delay`, loss, rate, or corruption, while plain veth links reject the same configuration and [`docs/manual/impairments.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/docs/manual/impairments.md#L1-L1) documents that these endpoints reject them. No unit test covers the stitched path.

**Suggested correction:** Mirror the `host`/`mgmt-net` endpoint rejection in `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve` &#40;for example in `buildVEthStitchSegment`, reusing the `declaresNetem` check from `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve`&#41;, add the failing cases to [`links/netem_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/netem_test.go#L1-L1), and update [`docs/manual/impairments.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/docs/manual/impairments.md#L1-L1) to state that veth-stitch node endpoints are supported instead of only &#34;node endpoints of veth links&#34;.


## P3 - `setDelay` writes only `TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64`/`JITTER64`, which older kernels silently ignore

**Location:** [netem/netem.go:115-123](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/netem/netem.go#L115-L123)

**Problem:** The base code wrote `Qopt.Latency`/`Qopt.Jitter` as ticks, which the `netem` qdisc has honored across all kernel versions. The head code leaves `Qopt.Latency`/`Qopt.Jitter` at zero and sets only `Netem.Latency64`/`Netem.Jitter64`; on kernels that predate the 64-bit `netem` latency attributes, the unknown attributes are silently skipped, leaving `delay` and `jitter` at zero.

**Trigger:** Deploying a topology with `delay`/`jitter` impairments on a `host` running a kernel without the `TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64`/`TCA_NETEM_JITTER64` attributes.

**Impact:** The `delay`/`jitter` impairment is silently absent on older kernels while the deploy succeeds; users get no error. This also makes the write path consistent with the pre-existing read path in [`cmd/tools_netem.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/cmd/tools_netem.go#L1-L1) &#40;which already read the 64-bit attributes&#41;, fixing an old inconsistency, but the kernel-version tradeoff is undocumented.

**Suggested correction:** Populate the tick-based `Qopt.Latency`/`Qopt.Jitter` alongside the 64-bit attributes so older kernels keep working &#40;modern kernels honor the later64-bit override&#41;, or document the minimum kernel version for `delay`/`jitter` in [`docs/manual/impairments.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/docs/manual/impairments.md#L1-L1).


## P4 - Schema permits `netem` on all extended link types although the runtime rejects non-veth types

**Location:** [schemas/clab.schema.json:1565-1567](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1565-L1567)

**Problem:** The `netem` property was added to the shared `link-endpoint` definition that `link-type-dummy`, `link-type-host`, `link-type-macvlan`, `link-type-mgmt-net`, `link-type-vxlan`, `link-type-vxlan-stitch`, `link-type-veth`, and `link-type-veth-stitch` all reference, but `checkNetemOnVeth` rejects `netem` on all of these except veth and veth-stitch.

**Trigger:** Validating any extended non-veth link with an endpoint `netem` key against [`clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1).

**Impact:** Editor validation and autocompletion accept topologies that the runtime always refuses with an error; the mismatch is cosmetic because the runtime message is clear.

**Suggested correction:** Optionally scope `netem` to a veth/veth-stitch-specific endpoint definition, or keep the permissive schema and note the runtime restriction in the `netem` property description.


## P4 - [`link_veth.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth.go#L1-L1) compares pseudo-node names against string literals instead of existing constants

**Location:** [links/link&#95;veth.go:70-73](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth.go#L70-L73)

**Problem:** The new guard uses `epr.Node == "host" \|\| epr.Node == "mgmt-net"`, while `LinkTypeHost` and `LinkTypeMgmtNet` already exist in [`links/link.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link.go#L1-L1) &#40;and `mgmtNetOwnerName` in [`links/link_mgmt-net.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_mgmt-net.go#L1-L1)&#41;.

**Trigger:** Any maintenance change to the pseudo-node names or the `netem` guard.

**Impact:** Minor maintainability cost; a rename or typo would silently break the rejection.

**Suggested correction:** Use `string(LinkTypeHost)`/`string(LinkTypeMgmtNet)` or dedicated pseudo-node-name constants in the check.


## Coverage

- All 28 changed paths in `manifest.json` were reviewed, including the full `diff.txt`, plus surrounding code&#58; [`links/link_veth_stitched.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth_stitched.go#L1-L1), [`links/generic_link_node.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/generic_link_node.go#L1-L1), [`core/apply.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/core/apply.go#L1-L1), [`core/clab.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/core/clab.go#L1-L1), [`cmd/tools_netem.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/cmd/tools_netem.go#L1-L1), [`nodes/sros/sros.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/nodes/sros/sros.go#L1-L1), and [`links/apply_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/apply_test.go#L1-L1).
- Source-only review&#58; no tests, formatter, or CI runs were executed; test coverage was assessed from source, and the robot suite assertions match the implementation&#39;s error strings but were not executed.
- go-tc v0.4.8 is not vendored in the snapshot, so the netlink serialization of Latency64/Jitter64/Rate64 was inferred from the go-tc API semantics rather than verified against library source; the kernel version range honoring the 64-bit latency attributes is not verifiable from the snapshot.
- The behavior of apply/deploy when a target node&#39;s container is currently stopped &#40;`ExecFunction` failure aborting the command&#41; was not traced end-to-end.
- `setRate` sets both Rate &#40;capped to `MaxUint32`&#41; and Rate64, which differs from iproute2 &#40;one or the other&#41;; on kernels lacking `TCA_NETEM_RATE64` the rate silently caps at 4 Gbit/s, which improves on the base truncation but was not verified against kernel precedence rules.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

174: diff --git a/core/link_netem.go b/core/link_netem.go
175: new file mode 100644
176: index 0000000..612b9a5
177: --- /dev/null
178: +++ b/core/link_netem.go
179: @@ -0,0 +1,111 @@
180: +package core
181: +
182: +import (
183: +	"context"
184: +	"errors"
185: +	"fmt"
186: +	"net"
187: +	"os/exec"
188: +
189: +	"github.com/charmbracelet/log"
190: +	"github.com/containernetworking/plugins/pkg/ns"
191: +	clablinks "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/links"
192: +	clabnetem "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/netem"
193: +)
194: +
195: +func linksEndpoints(links map[int]clablinks.Link) []clablinks.Endpoint {
196: +	var endpoints []clablinks.Endpoint
197: +	for _, link := range links {
198: +		endpoints = append(endpoints, link.GetEndpoints()...)
199: +	}
200: +
201: +	return endpoints
202: +}
203: +
204: +// applyLinkImpairments sets the link impairments of the given endpoints on their interfaces.
205: +// Impairments don't survive moving an interface to another namespace, so they have to be set
206: +// again whenever the interfaces of a node are restored.
207: +func applyLinkImpairments(ctx context.Context, endpoints []clablinks.Endpoint) error {
208: +	var errs []error
209: +	moduleLoaded := false
210: +
211: +	for _, endpoint := range endpoints {
212: +		netem := endpoint.GetNetem()
213: +		if netem == nil {
214: +			continue
215: +		}
216: +
217: +		if !moduleLoaded {
218: +			loadNetemModule(ctx)
219: +			moduleLoaded = true
220: +		}
221: +
222: +		if err := applyEndpointImpairment(ctx, endpoint, netem); err != nil {
223: +			errs = append(
224: +				errs,
225: +				fmt.Errorf("failed to set the link impairment of %s: %w", endpoint, err),
226: +			)
227: +		}
228: +	}
229: +
230: +	return errors.Join(errs...)
231: +}
232: +
233: +func applyEndpointImpairment(
234: +	ctx context.Context,
235: +	endpoint clablinks.Endpoint,
236: +	netem *clablinks.Netem,
237: +) error {
238: +	node := endpoint.GetNode()
239: +
240: +	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
241: +		nodeNS, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
242: +		if err != nil {
243: +			return err
244: +		}
245: +		defer nodeNS.Close()
246: +
247: +		tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(nodeNS.Fd()))
248: +		if err != nil {
249: +			return err
250: +		}
251: +		defer func() {
252: +			if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
253: +				log.Debugf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v", err)
254: +			}
255: +		}()
256: +
257: +		link, err := net.InterfaceByName(endpoint.GetIfaceName())
258: +		if err != nil {
259: +			return err
260: +		}
261: +
262: +		if err := clabnetem.ReplaceImpairments(
263: +			tcnl,
264: +			link,
265: +			netem.Delay,
266: +			netem.Jitter,
267: +			netem.Loss,
268: +			netem.Rate,
269: +			netem.Corruption,
270: +		); err != nil {
271: +			return err
272: +		}
273: +
274: +		log.Info(
275: +			"Set link impairments",
276: +			"node", node.GetShortName(),
277: +			"interface", endpoint.GetIfaceName(),
278: +		)
279: +
280: +		return nil
281: +	})
282: +}
283: +
284: +// loadNetemModule loads the sch_netem kernel module, which some distributions don't load on
285: +// their own.
286: +func loadNetemModule(ctx context.Context) {
287: +	if err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "modprobe", "sch_netem").Run(); err != nil {
288: +		log.Debug("failed to load the sch_netem kernel module", "err", err)
289: +	}
290: +}

327: diff --git a/docs/manual/impairments.md b/docs/manual/impairments.md
328: index 4960d7b..12b02d6 100644
329: --- a/docs/manual/impairments.md
330: +++ b/docs/manual/impairments.md
331: @@ -16,5 +16,49 @@ Labs are meant to be a reflection of real-world scenarios. To make simulated net
332:  These commands allow users to set, show and reset link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node and create labs simulating real-world network conditions.
333:  
334:  ```bash title="setting packet loss at 10% rate on eth1 interface of clab-netem-r1 node"
335:  containerlab tools netem set -n clab-netem-r1 -i eth1 --loss 10
336:  ```
337: +
338: +## Impairments in the topology
339: +
340: +Impairments can also be part of the topology, so they are set whenever the lab is deployed. The `netem` key of a link endpoint takes the same impairments as `tools netem set`, which apply to the packets the endpoint's interface sends:
341: +
342: +```yaml
343: +topology:
344: +  links:
345: +    - type: veth
346: +      endpoints:
347: +        - node: r1
348: +          interface: eth1
349: +          netem:
350: +            delay: 50ms
351: +            jitter: 5ms
352: +            loss: 0.5
353: +        - node: r2
354: +          interface: eth1
355: +          netem:
356: +            rate: 10000
357: +```
358: +
359: +| Key          | Meaning                                                               |
360: +| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
361: +| `delay`      | Time to delay the packets, e.g. `100ms`                               |
362: +| `jitter`     | Delay variation, e.g. `10ms`; needs a `delay`, at most `2.147483647s` |
363: +| `loss`       | Random packet loss in percent                                         |
364: +| `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s                                                  |
365: +| `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent                                   |
366: +
367: +Brief links take a list with the impairment of each endpoint, in the order of the endpoints. An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired:
368: +
369: +```yaml
370: +topology:
371: +  links:
372: +    - endpoints: ["r1:eth1", "r2:eth1"]
373: +      netem:
374: +        - delay: 50ms
375: +        - {}
376: +```
377: +
378: +Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of veth links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. Lab runtimes such as [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) don't apply them yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails.
379: +
380: +Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and when the lab is reconciled with a changed topology. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.

389:          ipv4: <NodeA-IPv4-Address>          # optional e.g. 192.168.0.1/24
390:          ipv6: <NodeA-IPv6-Address>          # optional e.g. 2001:db8::1/64
391: +        netem: <NodeA-Impairment>           # optional, see link impairments
392:        - node: <NodeB-Name>                  # mandatory
393:          interface: <NodeB-Interface-Name>   # mandatory
394:          mac: <NodeB-Interface-Mac>          # optional
395:          ipv4: <NodeB-IPv4-Address>          # optional
396:          ipv6: <NodeB-IPv6-Address>          # optional
397: +        netem: <NodeB-Impairment>           # optional
398:      mtu: <link-mtu>                         # optional
399:      vars: <link-variables>                  # optional (used in templating)
400:      labels: <link-labels>                   # optional (used in templating)
401:  ```
402:  
403: +The `netem` key sets [link impairments](impairments.md#impairments-in-the-topology) on the interface of an endpoint.
404: +
405:  ###### veth-stitch
406:  
407:  The veth-stitch link type transparently stitches its two endpoints by using a veth pair per node interface then each veth is joined with a transparent tc stitch to pass the traffic.
408:  
409:  ```mermaid

694: new file mode 100644
695: index 0000000..ea991e2
696: --- /dev/null
697: +++ b/links/netem.go
698: @@ -0,0 +1,126 @@
699: +package links
700: +
701: +import (
702: +	"fmt"
703: +	"math"
704: +	"slices"
705: +	"time"
706: +)
707: +
708: +// maxNetemJitter is the highest jitter the kernel accepts without capping it.
709: +const maxNetemJitter = math.MaxInt32 * time.Nanosecond
710: +
711: +// maxNetemRate is the highest rate in kbit/s that can be converted to bytes/s.
712: +const maxNetemRate = math.MaxUint64 / 1000
713: +
714: +// NetemRaw is the link impairment of an endpoint as defined in the topology file.
715: +// It applies to the packets the endpoint's interface sends.
716: +type NetemRaw struct {
717: +	Delay      string  `yaml:"delay,omitempty"`
718: +	Jitter     string  `yaml:"jitter,omitempty"`
719: +	Loss       float64 `yaml:"loss,omitempty"`
720: +	Rate       uint64  `yaml:"rate,omitempty"`
721: +	Corruption float64 `yaml:"corruption,omitempty"`
722: +}
723: +
724: +// Netem is the resolved link impairment of an endpoint.
725: +type Netem struct {
726: +	Delay      time.Duration
727: +	Jitter     time.Duration
728: +	Loss       float64
729: +	Rate       uint64
730: +	Corruption float64
731: +}
732: +
733: +// Resolve validates the impairment and returns nil if it sets nothing.
734: +func (r *NetemRaw) Resolve() (*Netem, error) {
735: +	if r == nil {
736: +		return nil, nil
737: +	}
738: +
739: +	netem := &Netem{Loss: r.Loss, Rate: r.Rate, Corruption: r.Corruption}
740: +
741: +	var err error
742: +	if netem.Delay, err = parseNetemDuration("delay", r.Delay); err != nil {
743: +		return nil, err
744: +	}
745: +	if netem.Jitter, err = parseNetemDuration("jitter", r.Jitter); err != nil {
746: +		return nil, err
747: +	}
748: +
749: +	if netem.Jitter != 0 && netem.Delay == 0 {
750: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem jitter cannot be set without setting delay")
751: +	}
752: +	if netem.Jitter > maxNetemJitter {
753: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem jitter must be at most %s", maxNetemJitter)
754: +	}
755: +	if !(netem.Loss >= 0 && netem.Loss <= 100) {
756: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem loss must be in the range between 0 and 100")
757: +	}
758: +	if !(netem.Corruption >= 0 && netem.Corruption <= 100) {
759: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem corruption must be in the range between 0 and 100")
760: +	}
761: +
762: +	if netem.Rate > maxNetemRate {
763: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem rate must be at most %d kbit/s", uint64(maxNetemRate))
764: +	}
765: +
766: +	if *netem == (Netem{}) {
767: +		return nil, nil
768: +	}
769: +
770: +	return netem, nil
771: +}
772: +
773: +func parseNetemDuration(name, value string) (time.Duration, error) {
774: +	if value == "" {
775: +		return 0, nil
776: +	}
777: +
778: +	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(value)
779: +	if err != nil {
780: +		return 0, fmt.Errorf("netem %s %q is not a duration, e.g. 100ms: %w", name, value, err)
781: +	}
782: +	if duration < 0 {
783: +		return 0, fmt.Errorf("netem %s %q must not be negative", name, value)
784: +	}
785: +
786: +	return duration, nil
787: +}
788: +
789: +func declaresNetem(e *EndpointRaw) bool {
790: +	return e != nil && e.Netem != nil && *e.Netem != (NetemRaw{})
791: +}
792: +
793: +// checkNetemOnVeth rejects link impairments on the endpoints of a link that is not a veth link.
794: +func checkNetemOnVeth(lt LinkType, endpoints ...*EndpointRaw) error {
795: +	if slices.ContainsFunc(endpoints, declaresNetem) {
796: +		return fmt.Errorf("netem is only supported on veth links, not on %s links", lt)
797: +	}
798: +
799: +	return nil
800: +}
801: +
802: +// DeclaresNetem reports whether the link sets a link impairment on any of its endpoints.
803: +func (ld *LinkDefinition) DeclaresNetem() bool {
804: +	var endpoints []*EndpointRaw
805: +
806: +	switch l := ld.Link.(type) {
807: +	case *LinkVEthRaw:
808: +		endpoints = l.Endpoints
809: +	case *LinkVEthStitchedRaw:
810: +		endpoints = l.Endpoints
811: +	case *LinkHostRaw:
812: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{l.Endpoint}
813: +	case *LinkMacVlanRaw:
814: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{l.Endpoint}
815: +	case *LinkMgmtNetRaw:
816: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{l.Endpoint}
817: +	case *LinkDummyRaw:
818: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{l.Endpoint}
819: +	case *LinkVxlanRaw:
820: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{&l.Endpoint}
821: +	}
822: +
823: +	return slices.ContainsFunc(endpoints, declaresNetem)
824: +}

857: +			want: &Netem{

859: +				Jitter:     5 * time.Millisecond,
860: +				Loss:       0.5,

862: +				Corruption: 0.1,
863: +			},
864: +		},

871: +			wantErr: "must not be negative",
872: +		},
873: +		"jitter without delay": {
874: +			raw:     &NetemRaw{Jitter: "5ms"},
875: +			wantErr: "jitter cannot be set without setting delay",
876: +		},
877: +		"jitter the kernel would cap": {

879: +			wantErr: "netem jitter must be at most 2.147483647s",
880: +		},
881: +		"loss above 100": {

883: +			wantErr: "loss must be in the range between 0 and 100",

972: +}

1310: +func TestNetemDurationPattern(t *testing.T) {
1311: +	b, err := os.ReadFile("clab.schema.json")
1312: +	if err != nil {
1313: +		t.Fatal(err)
1314: +	}
1315: +	var schema struct {
1316: +		Definitions map[string]struct {
1317: +			Properties map[string]struct {
1318: +				Pattern string
1319: +			}
1320: +		}
1321: +	}
1322: +	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &schema); err != nil {
1323: +		t.Fatal(err)
1324: +	}
1325: +	pattern := regexp.MustCompile(schema.Definitions["netem"].Properties["delay"].Pattern)
1326: +	for _, tc := range []struct {
1327: +		duration string
1328: +		valid    bool
1329: +	}{
1330: +		{duration: "100ms", valid: true},
1331: +		{duration: "1.5s", valid: true},
1332: +		{duration: "1m30s", valid: true},
1333: +		{duration: "250µs", valid: true},
1334: +		{duration: "250us", valid: true},
1335: +		{duration: "100"},
1336: +		{duration: "-5ms"},
1337: +		{duration: "5 ms"},
1338: +	} {
1339: +		t.Run(tc.duration, func(t *testing.T) {
1340: +			if got := pattern.MatchString(tc.duration); got != tc.valid {
1341: +				t.Errorf("schema accepts = %v, want %v", got, tc.valid)
1342: +			}
1343: +			d, err := time.ParseDuration(tc.duration)
1344: +			if tc.valid && (err != nil || d < 0) {
1345: +				t.Errorf("the schema accepts %q, but the topology doesn't: %v", tc.duration, err)
1346: +			}
1347: +		})
1348: +	}
1349: +}

1397: +*** Comments ***
1398: +This suite tests the link impairments (netem) defined in the topology: containerlab sets them when
1399: +the lab is deployed, sets them again when a node is started or restarted, and updates them on apply.
1400: +
1401: +
1402: +*** Settings ***
1403: +Library             OperatingSystem
1404: +Library             String
1405: +Resource            ../common.robot
1406: +
1407: +Suite Setup         Run Clab Command    destroy --name ${lab-name} --cleanup
1408: +Suite Teardown      Run Clab Command    destroy --name ${lab-name} --cleanup
1409: +
1410: +
1411: +*** Variables ***
1412: +${lab-name}                 link-netem
1413: +${runtime}                  docker
1414: +${topo}                     34-link-netem.clab.yml
1415: +${changed-vars}             34-link-netem.vars.changed.yml
1416: +${invalid-vars}             34-link-netem.vars.invalid.yml
1417: +${runtime-cli-exec-cmd}     docker exec
1418: +
1419: +
1420: +*** Test Cases ***
1421: +Deploy ${lab-name} lab
1422: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1423: +    ...    deploy -t ${CURDIR}/${topo}
1424: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1425: +    Should Contain    ${output}    Set link impairments
1426: +
1427: +Impairments of a brief link are set
1428: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    delay 50ms
1429: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    loss 1%
1430: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l2    eth1    rate 10Mbit
1431: +
1432: +Impairment of an extended link is set
1433: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l2    eth2    corrupt 2%
1434: +    Qdisc Should Not Contain    l1    eth2    netem
1435: +
1436: +Packets are delayed
1437: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
1438: +    ...    sudo ${runtime-cli-exec-cmd} clab-${lab-name}-l1 ping -c 3 -i 0.2 10.0.0.2
1439: +    Log    ${output}
1440: +    # a ping may be lost, so only the minimum RTT is checked
1441: +    ${min-rtt} =    Get Regexp Matches    ${output}    = ([0-9.]+)/    1
1442: +    Should Not Be Empty    ${min-rtt}
1443: +    Should Be True    ${min-rtt}[0] >= 45
1444: +
1445: +Restarted node gets its impairments again
1446: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1447: +    ...    restart -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --node l1
1448: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1449: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    delay 50ms
1450: +
1451: +Started node gets its impairments again
1452: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1453: +    ...    stop -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --node l2
1454: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1455: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1456: +    ...    start -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --node l2
1457: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1458: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l2    eth1    rate 10Mbit
1459: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l2    eth2    corrupt 2%
1460: +
1461: +Apply updates a changed impairment
1462: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1463: +    ...    apply -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --vars ${CURDIR}/${changed-vars}
1464: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1465: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    delay 200ms
1466: +
1467: +Apply rejects an invalid impairment
1468: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1469: +    ...    apply -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --vars ${CURDIR}/${invalid-vars}
1470: +    Should Not Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1471: +    Should Contain    ${output}    netem delay "50" is not a duration
1472: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    delay 200ms
1473: +
1474: +
1475: +*** Keywords ***
1476: +Run Clab Command
1477: +    [Arguments]    ${args}
1478: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
1479: +    ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} ${args} 2>&1
1480: +    Log    ${output}
1481: +    RETURN    ${rc}    ${output}
1482: +
1483: +Get Qdisc
1484: +    [Arguments]    ${node}    ${interface}
1485: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
1486: +    ...    sudo ip netns exec clab-${lab-name}-${node} tc qdisc show dev ${interface}
1487: +    Log    ${output}
1488: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1489: +    RETURN    ${output}
1490: +

1495: +

1498: +    ${qdisc} =    Get Qdisc    ${node}    ${interface}
1499: +    Should Not Contain    ${qdisc}    ${impairment}

To make simulated net\n332:  These commands allow users to set, show and reset link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node and create labs simulating real-world network conditions.\n333:  \n334:  ```bash title=\"setting packet loss at 10% rate on eth1 interface of clab-netem-r1 node\"\n335:  containerlab tools netem set -n clab-netem-r1 -i eth1 --loss 10\n336:  ```\n337: +\n338: +## Impairments in the topology\n339: +\n340: +Impairments can also be part of the topology, so they are set whenever the lab is deployed. The `netem` key of a link endpoint takes the same impairments as `tools netem set`, which apply to the packets the endpoint's interface sends:\n341: +\n342: +```yaml\n343: +topology:\n344: +  links:\n345: +    - type: veth\n346: +      endpoints:\n347: +        - node: r1\n348: +          interface: eth1\n349: +          netem:\n350: +            delay: 50ms\n351: +            jitter: 5ms\n352: +            loss: 0.5\n353: +        - node: r2\n354: +          interface: eth1\n355: +          netem:\n356: +            rate: 10000\n357: +```\n358: +\n359: +| Key          | Meaning                                                               |\n360: +| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n361: +| `delay`      | Time to delay the packets, e.g. `100ms`                               |\n362: +| `jitter`     | Delay variation, e.g. `10ms`; needs a `delay`, at most `2.147483647s` |\n363: +| `loss`       | Random packet loss in percent                                         |\n364: +| `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s                                                  |\n365: +| `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent                                   |\n366: +\n367: +Brief links take a list with the impairment of each endpoint, in the order of the endpoints. An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired:\n368: +\n369: +```yaml\n370: +topology:\n371: +  links:\n372: +    - endpoints: [\"r1:eth1\", \"r2:eth1\"]\n373: +      netem:\n374: +        - delay: 50ms\n375: +        - {}\n376: +```\n377: +\n378: +Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of veth links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. Lab runtimes such as [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) don't apply them yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails.\n379: +\n380: +Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and when the lab is reconciled with a changed topology. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.\n381: diff --git a/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md b/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\n382: a/docs/manual/impairments.md\n+++ b/docs/manual/impairments.md\n@@ -16,5 +16,49 @@ Labs are meant to be a reflection of real-world scenarios. To make simulated net\n These commands allow users to set, show and reset link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node and create labs simulating real-world network conditions.\n \n ```bash title=\"setting packet loss at 10% rate on eth1 interface of clab-netem-r1 node\"\n containerlab tools netem set -n clab-netem-r1 -i eth1 --loss 10\n ```\n+\n+## Impairments in the topology\n+\n+Impairments can also be part of the topology, so they are set whenever the lab is deployed. The `netem` key of a link endpoint takes the same impairments as `tools netem set`, which apply to the packets the endpoint's interface sends:\n+\n+```yaml\n+topology:\n+  links:\n+    - type: veth\n+      endpoints:\n+        - node: r1\n+          interface: eth1\n+          netem:\n+            delay: 50ms\n+            jitter: 5ms\n+            loss: 0.5\n+        - node: r2\n+          interface: eth1\n+          netem:\n+            rate: 10000\n+```\n+\n+| Key          | Meaning                                                               |\n+| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n+| `delay`      | Time to delay the packets, e.g. `100ms`                               |\n+| `jitter`     | Delay variation, e.g. `10ms`; needs a `delay`, at most `2.147483647s` |\n+| `loss`       | Random packet loss in percent                                         |\n+| `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s                                                  |\n+| `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent                                   |\n+\n+Brief links take a list with the impairment of each endpoint, in the order of the endpoints. An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired:\n+\n+```yaml\n+topology:\n+  links:\n+    - endpoints: [\"r1:eth1\", \"r2:eth1\"]\n+      netem:\n+        - delay: 50ms\n+        - {}\n+```\n+\n+Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of veth links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. Lab runtimes such as [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) don't apply them yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails.\n+\n+Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and when the lab is reconciled with a changed topology. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.\ndiff --git a/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md b/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\nindex 1: package core
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"context"
5: 	"errors"
6: 	"fmt"
7: 	"net"
8: 	"os/exec"
9: 
10: 	"github.com/charmbracelet/log"
11: 	"github.com/containernetworking/plugins/pkg/ns"
12: 	clablinks "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/links"
13: 	clabnetem "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/netem"
14: )
15: 
16: func linksEndpoints(links map[int]clablinks.Link) []clablinks.Endpoint {
17: 	var endpoints []clablinks.Endpoint
18: 	for _, link := range links {
19: 		endpoints = append(endpoints, link.GetEndpoints()...)
20: 	}
21: 
22: 	return endpoints
23: }
24: 
25: // applyLinkImpairments sets the link impairments of the given endpoints on their interfaces.
26: // Impairments don't survive moving an interface to another namespace, so they have to be set
27: // again whenever the interfaces of a node are restored.
28: func applyLinkImpairments(ctx context.Context, endpoints []clablinks.Endpoint) error {
29: 	var errs []error
30: 	moduleLoaded := false
31: 
32: 	for _, endpoint := range endpoints {
33: 		netem := endpoint.GetNetem()
34: 		if netem == nil {
35: 			continue
36: 		}
37: 
38: 		if !moduleLoaded {
39: 			loadNetemModule(ctx)
40: 			moduleLoaded = true
41: 		}
42: 
43: 		if err := applyEndpointImpairment(ctx, endpoint, netem); err != nil {
44: 			errs = append(
45: 				errs,
46: 				fmt.Errorf("failed to set the link impairment of %s: %w", endpoint, err),
47: 			)
48: 		}
49: 	}
50: 
51: 	return errors.Join(errs...)
52: }
53: 
54: func applyEndpointImpairment(
55: 	ctx context.Context,
56: 	endpoint clablinks.Endpoint,
57: 	netem *clablinks.Netem,
58: ) error {
59: 	node := endpoint.GetNode()
60: 
61: 	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
62: 		nodeNS, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
63: 		if err != nil {
64: 			return err
65: 		}
66: 		defer nodeNS.Close()
67: 
68: 		tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(nodeNS.Fd()))
69: 		if err != nil {
70: 			return err
71: 		}
72: 		defer func() {
73: 			if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
74: 				log.Debugf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v", err)
75: 			}
76: 		}()
77: 
78: 		link, err := net.InterfaceByName(endpoint.GetIfaceName())
79: 		if err != nil {
80: 			return err
81: 		}
82: 
83: 		if err := clabnetem.ReplaceImpairments(
84: 			tcnl,
85: 			link,
86: 			netem.Delay,
87: 			netem.Jitter,
88: 			netem.Loss,
89: 			netem.Rate,
90: 			netem.Corruption,
91: 		); err != nil {
92: 			return err
93: 		}
94: 
95: 		log.Info(
96: 			"Set link impairments",
97: 			"node", node.GetShortName(),
98: 			"interface", endpoint.GetIfaceName(),
99: 		)
100: 
101: 		return nil
102: 	})
103: }
104: 
105: // loadNetemModule loads the sch_netem kernel module, which some distributions don't load on
106: // their own.
107: func loadNetemModule(ctx context.Context) {
108: 	if err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "modprobe", "sch_netem").Run(); err != nil {
109: 		log.Debug("failed to load the sch_netem kernel module", "err", err)
110: 	}
111: }

1: package links
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"fmt"
5: 	"math"
6: 	"slices"
7: 	"time"
8: )
9: 
10: // maxNetemJitter is the highest jitter the kernel accepts without capping it.
11: const maxNetemJitter = math.MaxInt32 * time.Nanosecond
12: 
13: // maxNetemRate is the highest rate in kbit/s that can be converted to bytes/s.
14: const maxNetemRate = math.MaxUint64 / 1000
15: 
16: // NetemRaw is the link impairment of an endpoint as defined in the topology file.
17: // It applies to the packets the endpoint's interface sends.
18: type NetemRaw struct {

32: 	Corruption float64

35: // Resolve validates the impairment and returns nil if it sets nothing.
36: func (r *NetemRaw) Resolve() (*Netem, error) {
37: 	if r == nil {
38: 		return nil, nil
39: 	}
40: 
41: 	netem := &Netem{Loss: r.Loss, Rate: r.Rate, Corruption: r.Corruption}
42: 
43: 	var err error
44: 	if netem.Delay, err = parseNetemDuration("delay", r.Delay); err != nil {
45: 		return nil, err
46: 	}
47: 	if netem.Jitter, err = parseNetemDuration("jitter", r.Jitter); err != nil {
48: 		return nil, err
49: 	}
50: 
51: 	if netem.Jitter != 0 && netem.Delay == 0 {
52: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem jitter cannot be set without setting delay")
53: 	}
54: 	if netem.Jitter > maxNetemJitter {
55: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem jitter must be at most %s", maxNetemJitter)
56: 	}
57: 	if !(netem.Loss >= 0 && netem.Loss <= 100) {
58: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem loss must be in the range between 0 and 100")
59: 	}
60: 	if !(netem.Corruption >= 0 && netem.Corruption <= 100) {
61: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem corruption must be in the range between 0 and 100")
62: 	}
63: 
64: 	if netem.Rate > maxNetemRate {
65: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem rate must be at most %d kbit/s", uint64(maxNetemRate))
66: 	}
67: 
68: 	if *netem == (Netem{}) {
69: 		return nil, nil
70: 	}
71: 
72: 	return netem, nil
73: }

23: // ToLinkBriefRaw converts the raw link into a LinkBriefRaw.
24: func (r *LinkVEthRaw) ToLinkBriefRaw() *LinkBriefRaw {
25: 	lc := &LinkBriefRaw{
26: 		Endpoints:        []string{},
27: 		LinkCommonParams: r.LinkCommonParams,
28: 	}
29: 
30: 	for _, e := range r.Endpoints {
31: 		lc.Endpoints = append(lc.Endpoints, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", e.Node, e.Iface))
32: 	}
33: 
34: 	if slices.ContainsFunc(r.Endpoints, func(e *EndpointRaw) bool { return e.Netem != nil }) {
35: 		for _, e := range r.Endpoints {
36: 			lc.Netem = append(lc.Netem, e.Netem)
37: 		}
38: 	}
39: 
40: 	return lc
41: }

44: 	return LinkTypeVEth
45: }

47: // Resolve resolves the raw veth link definition into a Link interface that is implemented
48: // by a concrete LinkVEth struct.
49: // Resolving a veth link resolves its endpoints.
50: func (r *LinkVEthRaw) Resolve(params *ResolveParams) (Link, error) {
51: 	// filtered true means the link is in the filter provided by a user
52: 	// aka it should be resolved/created/deployed
53: 	filtered := isInFilter(params, r.Endpoints)
54: 	if !filtered {
55: 		return nil, nil
56: 	}
57: 
58: 	if r.fromBrief && r.briefDefaultLinkType(params) == LinkTypeVethStitch {
59: 		return NewVEthStitchedRawFromVEth(r).Resolve(params)
60: 	}
61: 
62: 	// create LinkVEth struct
63: 	l := NewLinkVEth()
64: 	l.LinkCommonParams = r.LinkCommonParams
65: 
66: 	// Normalize link vars to ensure JSON serialization compatibility
67: 	l.Vars = normalizeVars(l.Vars)
68: 
69: 	// resolve raw endpoints (epr) to endpoints (ep)
70: 	for _, epr := range r.Endpoints {
71: 		if (epr.Node == "host" || epr.Node == "mgmt-net") && declaresNetem(epr) {
72: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem is not supported on %s endpoints", epr.Node)
73: 		}
74: 
75: 		ep, err := epr.Resolve(params, l)
76: 		if err != nil {
77: 			return nil, err
78: 		}
79: 
80: 		// add endpoint to the link endpoints
81: 		l.Endpoints = append(l.Endpoints, ep)
82: 	}
83: 
84: 	// set default link mtu if MTU is unset
85: 	if l.MTU == 0 {
86: 		l.MTU = clabconstants.DefaultLinkMTU
87: 	}
88: 
89: 	return l, nil
90: }

93: func linkVEthRawFromLinkBriefRaw(lb *LinkBriefRaw) (*LinkVEthRaw, error) {
94: 	host, hostIf, node, nodeIf, err := extractHostNodeInterfaceData(lb, 0)
95: 	if err != nil {
96: 		return nil, err
97: 	}
98:

100: 		LinkCommonParams: lb.LinkCommonParams,
101: 		Endpoints: []*EndpointRaw{
102: 			NewEndpointRaw(host, hostIf, ""),
103: 			NewEndpointRaw(node, nodeIf, ""),
104: 		},
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	// populate vars

109: 		return nil, err
110: 	}
111: 
112: 	if len(lb.Netem) > len(link.Endpoints) {
113: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("number of netem entries exceeds the number of endpoints")
114: 	}
115: 	for i, netem := range lb.Netem {
116: 		link.Endpoints[i].Netem = netem
117: 	}

120: 	if link.MTU == 0 {
121: 		link.MTU = clabconstants.DefaultLinkMTU
122: 	}

124: 	return link, nil
125: }

148: 	for _, ep := range r.Endpoints {

175: func NewLinkVEth() *LinkVEth {
176: 	return &LinkVEth{
177: 		Endpoints: make([]Endpoint, 0, 2),
178: 	}
179: }
180: 
181: func (*LinkVEth) GetType() LinkType {
182: 	return LinkTypeVEth
183: }
184: 
185: func (l *LinkVEth) deployAEnd(ctx context.Context, idx int) error {
186: 	ep := l.Endpoints[idx]
187: 	// the peer Endpoint is the other of the two endpoints in the
188: 	// Endpoints slice. So do a +1 on the index and modulo operation
189: 	// to take care of the wrap around.
190: 	peerIdx := (idx + 1) % 2
191: 	peerEp := l.Endpoints[peerIdx]
192: 
193: 	log.Debugf("Creating Endpoint: %s ( --> %s )", ep, peerEp)
194: 
195: 	// build the netlink.Veth struct for the link provisioning
196: 	linkA := &netlink.Veth{
197: 		LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{
198: 			Name: ep.GetRandIfaceName(),
199: 			MTU:  l.MTU,
200: 			// Mac address is set later on
201: 		},
202: 		PeerName: peerEp.GetRandIfaceName(),
203: 		// PeerMac address is set later on
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	// add the link
207: 	err := netlink.LinkAdd(linkA)
208: 	if err != nil {
209: 		return err
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	// cleanup is a helper that removes the veth pair if a subsequent step fails
213: 	// after LinkAdd succeeded, preventing orphaned interfaces from blocking retries.
214: 	cleanup := func(err error) error {
215: 		if delErr := netlink.LinkDel(linkA); delErr != nil {
216: 			log.Debugf(
217: 				"failed to cleanup veth pair %s after error: %v",
218: 				ep.GetRandIfaceName(),
219: 				delErr,
220: 			)
221: 		}
222: 		return err
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	// disable TXOffloading
226: 	if err := clabutils.EthtoolTXOff(ep.GetRandIfaceName()); err != nil {
227: 		return cleanup(err)
228: 	}
229: 
230: 	// the link needs to be moved to the relevant network namespace
231: 	// and enabled (up). This is done via linkSetupFunc.
232: 	// based on the endpoint type the link setup function is different.
233: 	// linkSetupFunc is executed in a netns of a node.
234: 	// if the node is a regular namespace node
235: 	// add link to node, rename, set mac and Up
236: 	err = ep.GetNode().AddLinkToContainer(ctx, linkA,
237: 		SetNameMACAndUpInterface(linkA, ep))
238: 	if err != nil {
239: 		return cleanup(err)
240: 	}
241: 
242: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed
243: 
244: 	// e.g. host endpoints are nodeless, and therefore the B end of the veth link should
245: 	// be deployed right after the A end is deployed.
246: 	if peerEp.IsNodeless() {
247: 		return l.deployBEnd(ctx, peerIdx)
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	return nil
251: }
252: 
253: func (l *LinkVEth) deployBEnd(ctx context.Context, idx int) error {
254: 	ep := l.Endpoints[idx]
255: 	peerEp := l.Endpoints[(idx+1)%2]
256: 
257: 	log.Debugf("Assigning Endpoint: %s ( --> %s )", ep, peerEp)
258: 
259: 	// retrieve the netlink.Link for the provided Endpoint
260: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByName(ep.GetRandIfaceName())
261: 	if err != nil {
262: 		return err
263: 	}
264: 
265: 	// disable TXOffloading
266: 	if err := clabutils.EthtoolTXOff(ep.GetRandIfaceName()); err != nil {
267: 		return err
268: 	}
269: 
270: 	// Host endpoints already live in the current namespace; set them up in place.
271: 	// Other nodeless endpoints, such as the management bridge, still need their
272: 	// node-specific setup.
273: 	if ep.IsNodeless() && ep.GetNode().GetLinkEndpointType() == LinkEndpointTypeHost {
274: 		if err := SetNameMACAndUpInterface(link, ep)(nil); err != nil {
275: 			return err
276: 		}
277: 	} else if err = ep.GetNode().AddLinkToContainer(ctx, link,
278: 		SetNameMACAndUpInterface(link, ep)); err != nil {
279: 		return err
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed
283: 
284: 	if len(l.Endpoints) == 2 {
285: 		log.Infof("Created link: %s ▪┄┄▪ %s", l.Endpoints[0], l.Endpoints[1])
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	return nil
289: }
290: 
291: // getEndpointIndex returns the index of the ep endpoint belonging to l link.
292: // An error is returned when the ep is not part of the l's endpoints.
293: func (l *LinkVEth) getEndpointIndex(ep Endpoint) (int, error) {
294: 	for idx, e := range l.Endpoints {
295: 		if e == ep {
296: 			return idx, nil
297: 		}
298: 	}
299: 
300: 	// if the endpoint is not part of the link
301: 	// build a string list of endpoints and return a meaningful error
302: 	var epStrings []string
303: 	for _, e := range l.Endpoints {
304: 		epStrings = append(epStrings, e.String())
305: 	}
306: 
307: 	return -1, fmt.Errorf(
308: 		"endpoint %s does not belong to link [ %s ]",
309: 		ep.String(),
310: 		strings.Join(epStrings, ", "),
311: 	)
312: }
313: 
314: // Deploy deploys the veth link by creating the A and B sides of the veth pair independently
315: // based on the calling endpoint.
316: func (l *LinkVEth) Deploy(ctx context.Context, ep Endpoint) error {
317: 	// since each node calls deploy on its links, we need to make sure that we only deploy
318: 	// the link once, even if multiple nodes call deploy on the same link.
319: 	l.deployMutex.Lock()
320: 	defer l.deployMutex.Unlock()
321: 
322: 	// first we need to check that the provided ep is part of this link
323: 	idx, err := l.getEndpointIndex(ep)
324: 	if err != nil {
325: 		return err
326: 	}
327: 
328: 	// Retry transient netlink errors that can occur during concurrent link operations.
329: 	// deployAEnd cleans up partial state on failure, making each retry idempotent.
330: 	return retryTransientNetlink(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("deploy link %s", ep), func() error {
331: 		switch l.DeploymentState {
332: 		case LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed:
333: 			return l.deployBEnd(ctx, idx)
334: 		case LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed:
335: 			return nil
336: 		default:
337: 			return l.deployAEnd(ctx, idx)
338: 		}
339: 	})
340: }
341: 
342: func (*LinkVEth) PostDeploy(context.Context) error {
343: 	return nil
344: }
345: 
346: func (l *LinkVEth) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
347: 	l.deployMutex.Lock()
348: 	defer l.deployMutex.Unlock()
349: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateRemoved {
350: 		return nil
351: 	}
352: 	for _, ep := range l.GetEndpoints() {
353: 		err := ep.Remove(ctx)
354: 		if err != nil {
355: 			log.Debug(err)
356: 		}
357: 	}
358: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateRemoved
359: 	return nil
360: }
361: 
362: func (l *LinkVEth) GetEndpoints() []Endpoint {
363: 	return l.Endpoints
364: }
365: 
366: func (l *LinkVEth) GetRuntimeEndpoints() []Endpoint {
367: 	return l.GetEndpoints()
368: }

1: package links
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"context"
5: 	"crypto/sha1"
6: 	"encoding/hex"
7: 	"errors"
8: 	"fmt"
9: 	"slices"
10: 	"sort"
11: 	"sync"
12: 
13: 	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
14: 	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
15: 	"github.com/vishvananda/netlink"
16: )
17: 
18: type LinkVEthStitchedRaw struct {
19: 	LinkCommonParams `               yaml:",inline"`
20: 	Endpoints        []*EndpointRaw `yaml:"endpoints"`
21: }
22: 
23: func NewVEthStitchedRawFromVEth(v *LinkVEthRaw) *LinkVEthStitchedRaw {
24: 	return &LinkVEthStitchedRaw{
25: 		LinkCommonParams: v.LinkCommonParams,
26: 		Endpoints:        v.Endpoints,
27: 	}
28: }
29: 
30: func (*LinkVEthStitchedRaw) GetType() LinkType {
31: 	return LinkTypeVethStitch
32: }
33: 
34: func (r *LinkVEthStitchedRaw) Resolve(params *ResolveParams) (Link, error) {
35: 	if !isInFilter(params, r.Endpoints) {
36: 		return nil, nil
37: 	}
38: 
39: 	if err := validateVEthStitched(r); err != nil {
40: 		return nil, err
41: 	}
42: 
43: 	mtu := r.MTU
44: 	if mtu == 0 {
45: 		mtu = clabconstants.DefaultLinkMTU
46: 	}
47: 
48: 	l := &LinkVEthStitched{
49: 		LinkCommonParams: r.LinkCommonParams,
50: 		labName:          params.LabName,
51: 	}
52: 	l.MTU = mtu
53: 	l.Vars = normalizeVars(l.Vars)
54: 
55: 	segA, epA, err := buildVEthStitchSegment(params, l, r.Endpoints[0], mtu)
56: 	if err != nil {
57: 		return nil, err
58: 	}
59: 
60: 	segB, epB, err := buildVEthStitchSegment(params, l, r.Endpoints[1], mtu)
61: 	if err != nil {
62: 		return nil, err
63: 	}
64: 
65: 	l.segA, l.segB = segA, segB
66: 	l.epA, l.epB = epA, epB
67: 
68: 	return l, nil
69: }
70: 
71: // LinkVEthStitched is the resolved veth-stitch link: two veth segments
72: // (nodeA<->root-ns, nodeB<->root-ns) whose root-ns ends are joined by a tc stitch.
73: type LinkVEthStitched struct {
74: 	LinkCommonParams
75: 
76: 	lifecycleMutex sync.Mutex
77: 
78: 	// since the stitch veth lives in the root ns, we need to ensure altnames
79: 	// are per-lab unique.
80: 	labName string
81: 
82: 	segA *LinkVEth
83: 	segB *LinkVEth
84: 
85: 	// the two root-ns endpoints that get stitched together
86: 	epA Endpoint
87: 	epB Endpoint
88: }
89: 
90: func (*LinkVEthStitched) GetType() LinkType {
91: 	return LinkTypeVethStitch
92: }
93: 
94: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) GetEndpoints() []Endpoint {
95: 	return []Endpoint{l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.segB.Endpoints[0]}
96: }
97: 
98: // GetRuntimeEndpoints returns every material endpoint managed by the stitched link.
99: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) GetRuntimeEndpoints() []Endpoint {
100: 	return []Endpoint{l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.segB.Endpoints[0], l.epA, l.epB}
101: }
102: 
103: // Deploy creates the veth segment belonging to ep.
104: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) Deploy(ctx context.Context, ep Endpoint) error {
105: 	l.lifecycleMutex.Lock()
106: 	defer l.lifecycleMutex.Unlock()
107: 
108: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
109: 		return nil
110: 	}
111: 
112: 	var err error
113: 	switch ep {
114: 	case l.segA.Endpoints[0]:
115: 		err = l.segA.Deploy(ctx, ep)
116: 	case l.segB.Endpoints[0]:
117: 		err = l.segB.Deploy(ctx, ep)
118: 	default:
119: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %s does not belong to link [ %s, %s ]",
120: 			ep, l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.segB.Endpoints[0])
121: 	}
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return err
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed
127: 
128: 	if l.segA.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed &&
129: 		l.segB.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
130: 		return l.stitchSegments(ctx)
131: 	}
132: 
133: 	return nil
134: }
135: 
136: // PostDeploy tags the two root-ns far ends and joins them with tc.
137: // if they weren't already stitched in Deploy.
138: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) PostDeploy(ctx context.Context) error {
139: 	l.lifecycleMutex.Lock()
140: 	defer l.lifecycleMutex.Unlock()
141: 
142: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
143: 		return nil
144: 	}
145: 	if l.segA.DeploymentState != LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed ||
146: 		l.segB.DeploymentState != LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
147: 		return fmt.Errorf("cannot stitch veth segments before both are fully deployed")
148: 	}
149: 
150: 	return l.stitchSegments(ctx)
151: }
152: 
153: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) stitchSegments(ctx context.Context) error {
154: 	steps := []func() error{
155: 		func() error { return markFarEnd(l.epB, l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.labName) },
156: 		func() error { return markFarEnd(l.epA, l.segB.Endpoints[0], l.labName) },
157: 		func() error { return stitch(l.epA, l.epB) },
158: 		func() error { return stitch(l.epB, l.epA) },
159: 	}
160: 	for _, step := range steps {
161: 		if err := retryTransientNetlink(ctx, "veth-stitch", step); err != nil {
162: 			return err
163: 		}
164: 	}
165: 
166: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed
167: 
168: 	return nil
169: }
170: 
171: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
172: 	l.lifecycleMutex.Lock()
173: 	defer l.lifecycleMutex.Unlock()
174: 
175: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateRemoved {
176: 		return nil
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	err := errors.Join(l.segA.Remove(ctx), l.segB.Remove(ctx))
180: 
181: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateRemoved
182: 
183: 	return err
184: }
185: 
186: // buildVEthStitchSegment builds one veth segment: the real node endpoint plus a
187: // root-namespace far end named with a hash.
188: func buildVEthStitchSegment(
189: 	params *ResolveParams,
190: 	owner *LinkVEthStitched,
191: 	nodeEpRaw *EndpointRaw,
192: 	mtu int,
193: ) (*LinkVEth, Endpoint, error) {
194: 	seg := NewLinkVEth()
195: 	seg.MTU = mtu
196: 
197: 	nodeEp, err := nodeEpRaw.Resolve(params, owner)
198: 	if err != nil {
199: 		return nil, nil, err
200: 	}
201: 
202: 	// the far end sits in the root namespace (host node) with a short hash name
203: 	// that fits the 15 char name limit.
204: 	farName := stitchFarEndName(params.LabName, nodeEpRaw.Node, nodeEpRaw.Iface)
205: 	farGeneric := NewEndpointGeneric(GetHostLinkNode(), farName, seg)
206: 	farGeneric.MAC = nodeEp.GetMac()
207: 	farEp := NewEndpointHost(farGeneric)
208: 	seg.Endpoints = []Endpoint{nodeEp, farEp}
209: 
210: 	return seg, farEp, nil
211: }
212: 
213: func stitchFarEndName(labName, node, iface string) string {
214: 	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(labName + "\x00" + node + "\x00" + iface))
215: 	return "clab-s-" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:4]) // 7 + 8 = 15 chars
216: }
217: 
218: func markFarEnd(farEp, nodeEp Endpoint, labName string) error {
219: 	l, err := netlink.LinkByName(farEp.GetIfaceName())
220: 	if err != nil {
221: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to look up veth-stitch far end %q: %w", farEp.GetIfaceName(), err)
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	iface := nodeEp.GetIfaceAlias()
225: 	if iface == "" {
226: 		iface = nodeEp.GetIfaceName()
227: 	}
228: 
229: 	altName := StitchAltName(labName, nodeEp.GetNode().GetShortName(), iface)
230: 	if err := netlink.LinkAddAltName(l, altName); err != nil && !isAltNameNotSupportedErr(err) {
231: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to add veth-stitch altname %q: %w", altName, err)
232: 	}
233: 
234: 	return nil
235: }
236: 
237: func validateVEthStitched(r *LinkVEthStitchedRaw) error {
238: 	if len(r.Endpoints) != 2 {
239: 		return fmt.Errorf(
240: 			"veth-stitch links require exactly two endpoints, got %d",
241: 			len(r.Endpoints),
242: 		)
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	return nil
246: }
247: 
248: func (r *LinkVEthStitchedRaw) cleanupFilteredLink(
249: 	ctx context.Context,
250: 	labName string,
251: 	nodesFilter []string,
252: ) error {
253: 	return cleanupFilteredVethStitch(ctx, labName, nodesFilter, r.Endpoints)
254: }
255: 
256: func cleanupFilteredVethStitch(
257: 	ctx context.Context,
258: 	labName string,
259: 	nodesFilter []string,
260: 	endpoints []*EndpointRaw,
261: ) error {
262: 	for _, altName := range filteredVethStitchAltNames(labName, nodesFilter, endpoints) {
263: 		if err := RemoveOwnedInterface(ctx, GetHostLinkNode(), altName); err != nil {
264: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed cleaning up veth-stitch interface %q: %w", altName, err)
265: 		}
266: 	}
267: 
268: 	return nil
269: }
270: 
271: func filteredVethStitchAltNames(
272: 	labName string,
273: 	nodesFilter []string,
274: 	endpoints []*EndpointRaw,
275: ) []string {
276: 	names := make(map[string]struct{})
277: 	for _, ep := range endpoints {
278: 		if ep == nil || ep.Node == "" || ep.Iface == "" ||
279: 			!slices.Contains(nodesFilter, ep.Node) {
280: 			continue
281: 		}
282: 		names[StitchAltName(labName, ep.Node, ep.Iface)] = struct{}{}
283: 	}
284: 
285: 	result := make([]string, 0, len(names))
286: 	for name := range names {
287: 		result = append(result, name)
288: 	}
289: 	sort.Strings(result)
290: 
291: 	return result
292: }
293: 
294: // StitchAltName returns a unique name for veth-stitch links.
295: func StitchAltName(labName, node, iface string) string {
296: 	return "clab-stitch-" + clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(labName+"-"+node+"-"+iface)
297: }
298: 
299: // ToolsInterface returns the host-netns interface veth-stitch (and similar
300: // kinds) publish for node:iface under StitchAltName, or (nil, false) if none.
301: // Single seam for reporting/impairing the host side of the stitch.
302: func ToolsInterface(labName, node, iface string) (netlink.Link, bool) {
303: 	if labName == "" || node == "" || iface == "" {
304: 		return nil, false
305: 	}
306: 
307: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByName(StitchAltName(labName, node, iface))
308: 	if err != nil {
309: 		return nil, false
310: 	}
311: 
312: 	return link, true
313: }

(End of file - total 313 lines)

Reasoning
So `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve` does NOT check netem. The `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` check for host/mgmt-net endpoints happens before, but if the veth link is converted to a stitched link (via `NewVEthStitchedRawFromVEth(r).Resolve(params)` at line 58-60), the netem check happens in `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` before the stitched call? Actually the host/mgmt-net check is inside the `for _, epr := range r.Endpoints` loop AFTER the stitched branch. So a veth-stitch link with netem:
- `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` → filtered → `fromBrief && briefDefaultLinkType == LinkTypeVethStitch` → `NewVEthStitchedRawFromVEth(r).Resolve(params)` → `buildVEthStitchSegment` → `nodeEpRaw.Resolve(params, owner)` → sets Netem on the generic endpoint (via EndpointRaw.Resolve).

Then `applyLinkImpairments` would apply netem to the stitched segment's node endpoint. But applying netem qdisc on the node's interface in the stitched path: the node interface is a veth whose egress is tc-redirected to the stitch — adding a netem qdisc on the node interface would impair traffic... Actually with tc stitch (redirect action), traffic egressing the node interface is redirected to the far end. Does a netem qdisc on the node veth end interfere with the redirect? tc redirect at the qdisc level? The stitch uses tc mirred/redirect on the interface — the tc stitch is set via `stitch()` which likely adds a tc filter with mirred action on the far-end interface. A netem qdisc on the node-side interface replaces the default qdisc — mirred is an ingress/egress filter, not qdisc, so it might still work. Hmm.

But regardless: docs say only veth links support netem; stitched links (which are veth under the hood, resolved from brief veth links when nodes are sr-sim) would silently accept netem. Is that harmful or actually intended? Also, `DeclaresNetem` includes `LinkVEthStitchedRaw` — so a stitched link declaring netem would fail clabernetes deploys but work on local runtime. Inconsistent with docs. Also — importantly — is netem validated in the stitched path? Yes, `EndpointRaw.Resolve` calls `er.Netem.Resolve()` which validates. So impairment would be applied to the node interface. It may actually work in practice.

Hmm, but wait — the endpoints of a stitched link: `GetEndpoints()` returns `l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.segB.Endpoints[0]` — the node endpoints. Their Netem is set (from raw endpoint Resolve). So `applyLinkImpairments` would apply impairments to stitched link node endpoints. The docs claim only veth links support impairments — but veth-stitch is a variant of veth links and the endpoints carry netem through. Not clearly a bug; could work. It's an undocumented capability. I'd note as P4 maybe, or not at all. Let me not over-flag.

Now, more important: check the `mgmt-net` special node. In `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve`, the check for host/mgmt-net: `epr.Node == "host" || epr.Node == "mgmt-net"`. Are there constants? Let me check how mgmt-net endpoints are handled in EndpointRaw.Resolve.

16: // Endpoint is the interface that all endpoint types implement.
17: // Endpoints like bridge, host, veth and macvlan are the types implementing this interface.
18: type Endpoint interface {
19: 	// Deploy deploys this endpoint through its associated link.
20: 	Deploy(context.Context) error
21: 	GetNode() Node
22: 	SetNode(Node)
23: 	GetIfaceName() string
24: 	GetIfaceAlias() string
25: 	GetIfaceDisplayName() string
26: 	GetRandIfaceName() string
27: 	GetMac() net.HardwareAddr
28: 	GetIPv4Addr() netip.Prefix
29: 	GetIPv6Addr() netip.Prefix
30: 	GetNetem() *Netem
31: 	String() string
32: 	// GetLink retrieves the link that the endpoint is assigned to
33: 	GetLink() Link
34: 	// Verify verifies that the endpoint is valid and can be deployed
35: 	Verify(context.Context, *VerifyLinkParams) error
36: 	// HasSameNodeAndInterface returns true if an endpoint that implements this interface
37: 	// has the same node and interface name as the given endpoint.
38: 	HasSameNodeAndInterface(ept Endpoint) bool
39: 	Remove(context.Context) error
40: 	// Activate brings this endpoint's interface up in its current namespace.
41: 	Activate(context.Context) error
42: 	// IsNodeless returns true for the endpoints that has no explicit node defined in the topology.
43: 	// E.g. host endpoints, mgmt bridge endpoints.
44: 	// Because there is no node that would deploy this side of the link they should be deployed
45: 	// along
46: 	// with the A side of the veth link.
47: 	IsNodeless() bool
48: 	// Setters for ifaceName and Alias
49: 	SetIfaceName(string)
50: 	SetIfaceAlias(string)
51: 	IsRuntimeDiscovered() bool
52: 	// GetVars returns the endpoint-level vars.
53: 	GetVars() map[string]any
54: }
55: 
56: // EndpointGeneric is the generic endpoint struct that is used by all endpoint types.
57: type EndpointGeneric struct {
58: 	Node       Node
59: 	IfaceName  string
60: 	IfaceAlias string

62: 	Link     Link

67: 	Vars     map[string]any

69: }

71: func NewEndpointGeneric(node Node, iface string, link Link) *EndpointGeneric {
72: 	return &EndpointGeneric{
73: 		Node:       node,
74: 		IfaceName:  iface,
75: 		IfaceAlias: "",
76: 		// random name is generated for the endpoint to avoid name collisions
77: 		// when it is first deployed in the root namespace
78: 		randName: genRandomIfName(),
79: 		Link:     link,
80: 		Vars:     make(map[string]any),
81: 	}
82: }

147: func (e *EndpointGeneric) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
148: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
149: 		brSideEp, err := netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(e.GetIfaceName()))
150: 		_, notfound := err.(netlink.LinkNotFoundError)
151: 
152: 		switch {
153: 		case notfound:
154: 			// The netdev may already be gone while its bridge port is not, which is how OVS
155: 			// keeps a port whose name is not the topology interface name.
156: 			return removeBridgePort(e.GetNode(), e.GetIfaceName())
157: 		case err != nil:
158: 			return err
159: 		}
160: 		log.Debugf(
161: 			"Removing interface %q from namespace %q",
162: 			e.GetIfaceName(),
163: 			e.GetNode().GetShortName(),
164: 		)
165: 		if err = netlink.LinkDel(brSideEp); err != nil {
166: 			return err
167: 		}
168: 
169: 		return removeBridgePort(e.GetNode(), e.GetIfaceName())
170: 	})
171: }

173: // moveEndpoint moves the endpoint's interface into dst's namespace and transfers ownership.
174: // The interface is left in the DOWN state; callers that need it active should follow up with
175: // Endpoint.Activate once all endpoints are in place.
176: func moveEndpoint(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint, dst Node) error {
177: 	src := e.GetNode()
178: 	if src == nil {
179: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %q has no source node", e.GetIfaceName())
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	if dst == nil {
183: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %q has no destination node", e.GetIfaceName())
184: 	}
185: 
186: 	if src == dst {
187: 		return nil
188: 	}
189: 
190: 	if !slices.Contains(src.GetEndpoints(), e) {
191: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q does not own endpoint %q", src.GetShortName(), e.GetIfaceName())
192: 	}
193: 
194: 	for _, owned := range dst.GetEndpoints() {
195: 		if owned == e {
196: 			return fmt.Errorf(
197: 				"node %q already owns endpoint %q",
198: 				dst.GetShortName(),
199: 				e.GetIfaceName(),
200: 			)
201: 		}
202: 		if owned.GetIfaceName() == e.GetIfaceName() {
203: 			return fmt.Errorf(
204: 				"node %q already tracks interface %q",
205: 				dst.GetShortName(),
206: 				e.GetIfaceName(),
207: 			)
208: 		}
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	if err := ensureOwnershipAltName(ctx, e); err != nil {
212: 		return err
213: 	}
214: 
215: 	if err := moveLink(ctx, src, e.GetIfaceName(), dst); err != nil {
216: 		return err
217: 	}
218: 
219: 	if err := src.ReleaseEndpoint(e); err != nil {
220: 		return err
221: 	}
222: 	e.SetNode(dst)
223: 	if err := dst.AdoptEndpoint(e); err != nil {
224: 		e.SetNode(src)
225: 		_ = src.AdoptEndpoint(e)
226: 		return fmt.Errorf(
227: 			"endpoint %q moved but destination ownership update failed: %w",
228: 			e.GetIfaceName(),
229: 			err,
230: 		)
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return nil
234: }

236: // Activate brings the endpoint's interface up in its current namespace.
237: func (e *EndpointGeneric) Activate(ctx context.Context) error {
238: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
239: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
240: 		if err != nil {
241: 			return err
242: 		}
243: 		return netlink.LinkSetUp(link)
244: 	})
245: }
246: 
247: func ensureOwnershipAltName(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) error {
248: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
249: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
250: 		if err != nil {
251: 			return err
252: 		}
253: 
254: 		return addOwnershipAltName(link, e)
255: 	})
256: }
257: 
258: // HasSameNodeAndInterface returns true if the given endpoint has the same node and interface name
259: // as the `ept` endpoint.
260: func (e *EndpointGeneric) HasSameNodeAndInterface(ept Endpoint) bool {
261: 	return e.Node == ept.GetNode() && e.IfaceName == ept.GetIfaceName()
262: }
263: 
264: func (e *EndpointGeneric) String() string {
265: 	ifDisplayName := e.IfaceName
266: 	if e.IfaceAlias != "" {
267: 		ifDisplayName += fmt.Sprintf(" (%s)", e.IfaceAlias)
268: 	}
269: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", e.Node.GetShortName(), ifDisplayName)
270: }
271: 
272: // CheckEndpointUniqueness checks that the given endpoint appears only once for the node
273: // it is assigned to.
274: func CheckEndpointUniqueness(e Endpoint) error {
275: 	for _, ept := range e.GetNode().GetEndpoints() {
276: 		if e == ept {
277: 			// since node contains all endpoints including the one we are checking
278: 			// we skip it
279: 			continue
280: 		}
281: 		// if `e` has the same node and interface name as `ept` then we have a duplicate
282: 		if e.HasSameNodeAndInterface(ept) {
283: 			return fmt.Errorf("duplicate endpoint %s", e)
284: 		}
285: 	}
286: 
287: 	return nil
288: }
289: 
290: // CheckEndpointExists checks that a certain
291: // interface exists in the network namespace of the given node.
292: func CheckEndpointExists(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) error {
293: 	err := CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet(ctx, e)
294: 	if err == nil {
295: 		return fmt.Errorf("interface %q does not exist", e.String())
296: 	}
297: 	return nil
298: }
299: 
300: // CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet verifies that the interface referenced in the
301: // provided endpoint does not yet exist in the referenced node.
302: func CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) error {
303: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
304: 		// we expect a netlink.LinkNotFoundError when querying for
305: 		// the interface with the given endpoints name
306: 		var err error
307: 		_, err = netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
308: 
309: 		if _, notfound := err.(netlink.LinkNotFoundError); notfound {
310: 			return nil
311: 		}
312: 
313: 		return fmt.Errorf(
314: 			"interface %s is defined via topology but already exists: %v",
315: 			e.String(),
316: 			err,
317: 		)
318: 	})
319: }
320: 
321: func moveLink(ctx context.Context, src Node, ifaceName string, dst Node) error {
322: 	return src.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
323: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(ifaceName)
324: 		if err != nil {
325: 			return err
326: 		}
327: 
328: 		if err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {
329: 			return err
330: 		}
331: 
332: 		return dst.AddLinkToContainer(ctx, link, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
333: 			return nil
334: 		})
335: 	})
336: }

254: 		return nil, err
255: 	}
256: 	if err := c.SyncMgmtHostRoutes(ctx); err != nil {
257: 		return nil, err
258: 	}
259: 
260: 	if _, err := c.finalize(ctx, options.exportTemplate, options.graph); err != nil {
261: 		return nil, err
262: 	}
263: 
264: 	return applyResultFromPlan(plan), nil
265: }

267: func (c *CLab) checkApplyTopologyDefinition(ctx context.Context) error {
268: 	params := *clablinks.NewVerifyLinkParams()
269: 	if len(c.Endpoints) > 0 {
270: 		runtime := c.globalRuntime()
271: 		if runtime == nil {
272: 			return fmt.Errorf("container runtime is not initialized")
273: 		}
274: 		config := runtime.Config()
275: 		if config.VerifyLinkParams != nil {
276: 			params = *config.VerifyLinkParams
277: 		}
278: 	}
279: 	params.AllowExistingEndpoint = true
280: 	if err := c.verifyLinks(ctx, &params); err != nil {
281: 		return err
282: 	}
283: 
284: 	if err := c.verifyRootNetNSLinks(); err != nil {
285: 		return err
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
289: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].CheckDeploymentConditions(ctx); err != nil {
290: 			return err
291: 		}
292: 	}
293: 
294: 	if err := c.verifyDuplicateAddresses(); err != nil {
295: 		return err
296: 	}
297: 
298: 	return c.verifyTailscaleProxy()
299: }
300: 
301: func (c *CLab) prepareApply(
302: 	ctx context.Context,
303: 	addedNodes []string,
304: 	skipLabDirFileACLs bool,
305: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
306: ) error {
307: 	existing := c.collectExistingManagementAddresses(currentNodes)
308: 	if err := c.prepareLabManagementNetwork(ctx, existing...); err != nil {
309: 		return err
310: 	}
311: 
312: 	if err := c.prepareDeployArtifacts(ctx, skipLabDirFileACLs); err != nil {
313: 		return err
314: 	}
315: 
316: 	for _, nodeName := range addedNodes {
317: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].PullImage(ctx); err != nil {
318: 			return err
319: 		}
320: 	}
321: 
322: 	return nil
323: }

325: func (*CLab) removeApplyLinkEndpoints(ctx context.Context, links []clablinks.Link) error {
326: 	for _, link := range links {
327: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
328: 			if err := clablinks.RemoveOwnedInterface(
329: 				ctx,
330: 				ep.GetNode(),
331: 				ep.GetIfaceName(),
332: 			); err != nil {
333: 				return err
334: 			}
335: 		}
336: 	}
337: 
338: 	return nil
339: }

341: // try to preserve the existing addressing instead of reallocation.
342: func (c *CLab) collectExistingManagementAddresses(
343: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
344: ) []clabtypes.ExistingAddress {
345: 	var existing []clabtypes.ExistingAddress
346: 	for name, group := range currentNodes {
347: 		for _, ctr := range group.containers {
348: 			if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(ctr.NetworkName).Network != ctr.NetworkName {
349: 				continue
350: 			}
351: 			for _, value := range []string{ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv4addr, ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv6addr} {
352: 				if ip, err := netip.ParseAddr(value); err == nil {
353: 					existing = append(
354: 						existing,
355: 						clabtypes.ExistingAddress{NodeName: name, ContainerID: ctr.ID, Address: ip},
356: 					)
357: 				}
358: 			}
359: 		}
360: 	}
361: 	return existing
362: }

250: func checkLabRuntimeCommandSupport(cobraCmd *cobra.Command, runtimeName string) error {
251: 	if !clablabruntime.IsLabRuntimeName(runtimeName) {
252: 		return nil
253: 	}
254: 
255: 	for cmd := cobraCmd; cmd != nil; cmd = cmd.Parent() {
256: 		if _, ok := labRuntimeUnsupportedCommands[cmd.Name()]; ok {
257: 			return fmt.Errorf("the %q command is not supported with lab runtime %q",
258: 				cmd.Name(), runtimeName)
259: 		}
260: 	}
261: 
262: 	if getCommandPath(cobraCmd) == "graph" && !graphRendersFromTopologyFile(cobraCmd) {
263: 		return fmt.Errorf(
264: 			"the %q command needs running containers with lab runtime %q unless it renders "+
265: 				"from the topology file alone; use --offline, --dot, --mermaid or --drawio",
266: 			"graph", runtimeName)
267: 	}
268: 
269: 	var unsupported []string
270: 	for _, flagName := range labRuntimeUnsupportedFlags[getCommandPath(cobraCmd)] {
271: 		if labRuntimeFlagWasSet(cobraCmd, flagName) {
272: 			unsupported = append(unsupported, "--"+flagName)
273: 		}
274: 	}
275: 	if len(unsupported) != 0 {
276: 		sort.Strings(unsupported)
277: 
278: 		return fmt.Errorf(
279: 			"flag(s) %s are not supported with the %q command and lab runtime %q",
280: 			strings.Join(unsupported, ", "),
281: 			cobraCmd.Name(),
282: 			runtimeName,
283: 		)
284: 	}
285: 
286: 	return nil
287: }

289: func graphRendersFromTopologyFile(cobraCmd *cobra.Command) bool {

297:

146: func (c *CLab) setMgmtBridgeFromRuntime(

151: 	}

223: func runtimeContainerLess(a, b clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {
224: 	// internal holders own the network namespace of the other containers in the group,
225: 	// so they sort first to be deleted last.
226: 	aInternal := a.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true"
227: 	bInternal := b.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true"
228: 	if aInternal != bInternal {
229: 		return aInternal
230: 	}
231: 
232: 	aName := runtimeContainerNodeName(a)
233: 	bName := runtimeContainerNodeName(b)
234: 
235: 	aOrder := runtimeComponentSortOrder(aName)
236: 	bOrder := runtimeComponentSortOrder(bName)
237: 	if aOrder != bOrder {
238: 		return aOrder < bOrder
239: 	}
240: 
241: 	return aName < bName
242: }
243: 
244: func runtimeComponentSortOrder(name string) int {
245: 	idx := strings.LastIndex(name, "-")
246: 	if idx < 0 || idx == len(name)-1 {
247: 		return 0
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	slot := strings.ToUpper(name[idx+1:])
251: 	if len(slot) == 1 && slot[0] >= 'A' && slot[0] <= 'Z' {
252: 		return 100 - int(slot[0])
253: 	}
254: 
255: 	var n int
256: 	for _, r := range slot {
257: 		if r < '0' || r > '9' {
258: 			return 0
259: 		}
260: 		n = n*10 + int(r-'0')
261: 	}
262: 
263: 	return n
264: }
