55: 		link.MTU = clabconstants.DefaultLinkMTU
56: 	}
57: 
58: 	return link, nil
59: }
60: 
61: func (r *LinkMacVlanRaw) Resolve(params *ResolveParams) (Link, error) {
62: 	if err := checkNetemOnVeth(LinkTypeMacVLan, r.Endpoint); err != nil {
63: 		return nil, err
64: 	}
65: 
66: 	var err error
67: 	// filtered true means the link is in the filter provided by a user
68: 	// aka it should be resolved/created/deployed
69: 	filtered := isInFilter(params, []*EndpointRaw{r.Endpoint})
70: 	if !filtered {
71: 		return nil, nil
72: 	}
73: 
74: 	// create the MacVlan Link
75: 	link := &LinkMacVlan{
76: 		LinkCommonParams: r.LinkCommonParams,
77: 	}
78: 
79: 	// Normalize link vars to ensure JSON serialization compatibility
80: 	link.Vars = normalizeVars(link.Vars)
81: 
82: 	// create the host side MacVlan Endpoint
83: 	link.HostEndpoint = NewEndpointMacVlan(
84: 		NewEndpointGeneric(GetHostLinkNode(), r.HostInterface, link),
85: 	)
86: 
87: 	// populate the host interfaces mac address
88: 	hostLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(r.HostInterface)
89: 	if err != nil {
90: 		return nil, err
91: 	}
92: 	link.HostEndpoint.MAC = hostLink.Attrs().HardwareAddr
93: 
94: 	// parse the MacVlanMode
95: 	mode, err := MacVlanModeParse(r.Mode)
96: 	if err != nil {
97: 		return nil, err
98: 	}
99: 	// set the mode in the link struct
100: 	link.Mode = mode
101: 	// resolve the endpoint
102: 	link.NodeEndpoint, err = r.Endpoint.Resolve(params, link)
103: 	if err != nil {
104: 		return nil, err
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	// propagate the parent interface MTU to the link
108: 	// because the macvlan interface MTU is inherited from
109: 	// its parent interface
110: 	link.MTU, err = link.GetParentInterfaceMTU()
111: 	if err != nil {
112: 		return nil, err
113: 	}
114: 
115: 	return link, nil
116: }
117: 
118: type LinkMacVlan struct {
119: 	LinkCommonParams
120: 	HostEndpoint *EndpointMacVlan
121: 	NodeEndpoint Endpoint
122: 	Mode         MacVlanMode
123: }
124: 
125: func (*LinkMacVlan) GetType() LinkType {
126: 	return LinkTypeMacVLan
127: }
128: 
129: func (l *LinkMacVlan) GetParentInterfaceMTU() (int, error) {
130: 	hostLink, err := netlink.LinkByName(l.HostEndpoint.GetIfaceName())
131: 	if err != nil {
132: 		return 0, err
133: 	}
134: 	return hostLink.Attrs().MTU, nil
135: }
136: 
137: func (l *LinkMacVlan) Deploy(ctx context.Context, _ Endpoint) error {
138: 	// lookup the parent host interface
139: 	parentInterface, err := netlink.LinkByName(l.HostEndpoint.GetIfaceName())
140: 	if err != nil {
141: 		return err
142: 	}
143: 
144: 	log.Infof("Creating MACVLAN link: %s <--> %s", l.HostEndpoint, l.NodeEndpoint)
145: 
146: 	// build Netlink Macvlan struct
147: 	link := &netlink.Macvlan{
148: 		LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{
149: 			Name:        l.NodeEndpoint.GetRandIfaceName(),
150: 			ParentIndex: parentInterface.Attrs().Index,
151: 		},
152: 		Mode: l.Mode.ToNetlinkMode(),
153: 	}
154: 	// add the link in the Host NetNS
155: 	err = netlink.LinkAdd(link)
156: 	if err != nil {
157: 		return err
158: 	}
159: 
160: 	// retrieve the Link by name
161: 	mvInterface, err := netlink.LinkByName(l.NodeEndpoint.GetRandIfaceName())
162: 	if err != nil {
163: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to lookup %q: %v", l.NodeEndpoint.GetRandIfaceName(), err)
164: 	}
165: 
166: 	// enable promiscuous mode
167: 	err = netlink.SetPromiscOn(mvInterface)
168: 	if err != nil {
169: 		return fmt.Errorf(
170: 			"failed setting promiscuous mode for interface %s (%s:%s): %v",
171: 			l.NodeEndpoint.GetRandIfaceName(),
172: 			l.NodeEndpoint.GetNode().GetShortName(),
173: 			l.NodeEndpoint.GetIfaceName(),
174: 			err,
175: 		)
176: 	}
177: 
178: 	// add the link to the Node Namespace
179: 	err = l.NodeEndpoint.GetNode().AddLinkToContainer(ctx, mvInterface,
180: 		SetNameMACAndUpInterface(mvInterface, l.NodeEndpoint))
181: 	return err
182: }
183: 
184: func (*LinkMacVlan) PostDeploy(context.Context) error {
185: 	return nil
186: }
187: 
188: func (l *LinkMacVlan) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
189: 	// check Deployment state, if the Link was already
190: 	// removed via e.g. the peer node
191: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateRemoved {
192: 		return nil
193: 	}
194: 	// trigger link removal via the NodeEndpoint
195: 	err := l.NodeEndpoint.Remove(ctx)
196: 	if err != nil {
197: 		log.Debug(err)
198: 	}
199: 	// adjust the Deployment status to reflect the removal
200: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateRemoved
201: 	return nil
202: }
203: 
204: func (l *LinkMacVlan) GetEndpoints() []Endpoint {
205: 	return []Endpoint{
206: 		l.NodeEndpoint,
207: 		l.HostEndpoint,
208: 	}
209: }
210: 
211: func (l *LinkMacVlan) GetRuntimeEndpoints() []Endpoint {
212: 	return []Endpoint{l.NodeEndpoint}
213: }

215: type MacVlanMode string
216: 
217: const (
218: 	MacVlanModeBridge   = "bridge"
219: 	MacVlanModeVepa     = "vepa"
220: 	MacVlanModePassthru = "passthru"
221: 	MacVlanModePrivate  = "private"
222: 	MacVlanModeSource   = "source"
223: )
224: 
225: func MacVlanModeParse(s string) (MacVlanMode, error) {
226: 	switch s {
227: 	case MacVlanModeBridge:
228: 		return MacVlanModeBridge, nil
229: 	case MacVlanModeVepa:
230: 		return MacVlanModeVepa, nil
231: 	case MacVlanModePassthru:
232: 		return MacVlanModePassthru, nil
233: 	case MacVlanModePrivate:
234: 		return MacVlanModePrivate, nil
235: 	case MacVlanModeSource:
236: 		return MacVlanModeSource, nil
237: 	case "":
238: 		return MacVlanModeBridge, nil
239: 	}
240: 	return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown MacVlanMode %q", s)
241: }
242: 
243: func (m MacVlanMode) ToNetlinkMode() netlink.MacvlanMode {
244: 	var mode netlink.MacvlanMode
245: 	switch m {
246: 	case MacVlanModeBridge:
247: 		mode = netlink.MACVLAN_MODE_BRIDGE
248: 	case MacVlanModePassthru:
249: 		mode = netlink.MACVLAN_MODE_PASSTHRU
250: 	case MacVlanModeVepa:
251: 		mode = netlink.MACVLAN_MODE_VEPA
252: 	case MacVlanModePrivate:
253: 		mode = netlink.MACVLAN_MODE_PRIVATE
254: 	case MacVlanModeSource:
255: 		mode = netlink.MACVLAN_MODE_SOURCE
256: 	}
257: 	return mode
258: }

21: // NewTC returns a new tc client opened for a given network namespace.
22: // Must be closed after use.
23: func NewTC(ns int) (*tc.Tc, error) {
24: 	tcnl, err := tc.Open(&tc.Config{
25: 		NetNS: ns,
26: 	})
27: 	if err != nil {
28: 		return nil, err
29: 	}
30: 
31: 	return tcnl, nil
32: }

34: // SetImpairments sets the impairments on the given interface of a node and returns its qdisc.
35: func SetImpairments(tcnl *tc.Tc, nodeName string, link *net.Interface, delay, jitter time.Duration,
36: 	loss float64, rate uint64, probability float64,
37: ) (*tc.Object, error) {
38: 	err := ReplaceImpairments(tcnl, link, delay, jitter, loss, rate, probability)
39: 	if err != nil {
40: 		return nil, err
41: 	}
42: 
43: 	// get qdisc of an interface after we set it
44: 	qdiscs, err := tcnl.Qdisc().Get()
45: 	if err != nil {
46: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("could not get all qdiscs: %v", err)
47: 	}
48: 
49: 	for idx := range qdiscs {
50: 		if qdiscs[idx].Ifindex == uint32(link.Index) {
51: 			return &qdiscs[idx], nil
52: 		}
53: 	}
54: 
55: 	return nil, fmt.Errorf("could not find qdisc for interface %q", link.Name)
56: }
57: 
58: // ReplaceImpairments sets the impairments on the given interface, replacing the ones it has.
59: func ReplaceImpairments(tcnl *tc.Tc, link *net.Interface, delay, jitter time.Duration,
60: 	loss float64, rate uint64, probability float64,
61: ) error {
62: 	err := tcnl.SetOption(netlink.ExtendedAcknowledge, true)
63: 	if err != nil {
64: 		return fmt.Errorf("could not set option ExtendedAcknowledge: %v", err)
65: 	}
66: 
67: 	qdisc := tc.Object{
68: 		Msg: tc.Msg{
69: 			Family:  unix.AF_UNSPEC,

147: func (e *EndpointGeneric) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
148: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
149: 		brSideEp, err := netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(e.GetIfaceName()))
150: 		_, notfound := err.(netlink.LinkNotFoundError)
151: 
152: 		switch {
153: 		case notfound:
154: 			// The netdev may already be gone while its bridge port is not, which is how OVS
155: 			// keeps a port whose name is not the topology interface name.
156: 			return removeBridgePort(e.GetNode(), e.GetIfaceName())
157: 		case err != nil:
158: 			return err
159: 		}
160: 		log.Debugf(
161: 			"Removing interface %q from namespace %q",
162: 			e.GetIfaceName(),
163: 			e.GetNode().GetShortName(),
164: 		)
165: 		if err = netlink.LinkDel(brSideEp); err != nil {
166: 			return err
167: 		}
168: 
169: 		return removeBridgePort(e.GetNode(), e.GetIfaceName())
170: 	})
171: }

173: // moveEndpoint moves the endpoint's interface into dst's namespace and transfers ownership.
174: // The interface is left in the DOWN state; callers that need it active should follow up with
175: // Endpoint.Activate once all endpoints are in place.
176: func moveEndpoint(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint, dst Node) error {
177: 	src := e.GetNode()
178: 	if src == nil {
179: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %q has no source node", e.GetIfaceName())
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	if dst == nil {
183: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %q has no destination node", e.GetIfaceName())
184: 	}
185: 
186: 	if src == dst {
187: 		return nil
188: 	}
189: 
190: 	if !slices.Contains(src.GetEndpoints(), e) {
191: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q does not own endpoint %q", src.GetShortName(), e.GetIfaceName())
192: 	}
193: 
194: 	for _, owned := range dst.GetEndpoints() {
195: 		if owned == e {
196: 			return fmt.Errorf(
197: 				"node %q already owns endpoint %q",
198: 				dst.GetShortName(),
199: 				e.GetIfaceName(),
200: 			)
201: 		}
202: 		if owned.GetIfaceName() == e.GetIfaceName() {
203: 			return fmt.Errorf(
204: 				"node %q already tracks interface %q",
205: 				dst.GetShortName(),
206: 				e.GetIfaceName(),
207: 			)
208: 		}
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	if err := ensureOwnershipAltName(ctx, e); err != nil {
212: 		return err
213: 	}
214: 
215: 	if err := moveLink(ctx, src, e.GetIfaceName(), dst); err != nil {
216: 		return err
217: 	}
218: 
219: 	if err := src.ReleaseEndpoint(e); err != nil {
220: 		return err
221: 	}
222: 	e.SetNode(dst)
223: 	if err := dst.AdoptEndpoint(e); err != nil {
224: 		e.SetNode(src)
225: 		_ = src.AdoptEndpoint(e)
226: 		return fmt.Errorf(
227: 			"endpoint %q moved but destination ownership update failed: %w",
228: 			e.GetIfaceName(),
229: 			err,
230: 		)
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	return nil
234: }

237: func (e *EndpointGeneric) Activate(ctx context.Context) error {
238: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
239: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
240: 		if err != nil {
241: 			return err
242: 		}
243: 		return netlink.LinkSetUp(link)
244: 	})
245: }

249: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
250: 		if err != nil {

252: 		}
253: 
254: 		return addOwnershipAltName(link, e)
255: 	})
256: }

272: // CheckEndpointUniqueness checks that the given endpoint appears only once for the node
273: // it is assigned to.
274: func CheckEndpointUniqueness(e Endpoint) error {
275: 	for _, ept := range e.GetNode().GetEndpoints() {
276: 		if e == ept {
277: 			// since node contains all endpoints including the one we are checking
278: 			// we skip it
279: 			continue
280: 		}
281: 		// if `e` has the same node and interface name as `ept` then we have a duplicate
282: 		if e.HasSameNodeAndInterface(ept) {
283: 			return fmt.Errorf("duplicate endpoint %s", e)
284: 		}
285: 	}
286: 
287: 	return nil
288: }
289: 
290: // CheckEndpointExists checks that a certain
291: // interface exists in the network namespace of the given node.
292: func CheckEndpointExists(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) error {
293: 	err := CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet(ctx, e)
294: 	if err == nil {
295: 		return fmt.Errorf("interface %q does not exist", e.String())
296: 	}
297: 	return nil
298: }
299: 
300: // CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet verifies that the interface referenced in the
301: // provided endpoint does not yet exist in the referenced node.
302: func CheckEndpointDoesNotExistYet(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) error {
303: 	return e.GetNode().ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
304: 		// we expect a netlink.LinkNotFoundError when querying for
305: 		// the interface with the given endpoints name
306: 		var err error
307: 		_, err = netlink.LinkByName(e.GetIfaceName())
308: 
309: 		if _, notfound := err.(netlink.LinkNotFoundError); notfound {
310: 			return nil
311: 		}
312: 
313: 		return fmt.Errorf(
314: 			"interface %s is defined via topology but already exists: %v",
315: 			e.String(),
316: 			err,
317: 		)
318: 	})
319: }
320: 
321: func moveLink(ctx context.Context, src Node, ifaceName string, dst Node) error {
322: 	return src.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
323: 		link, err := netlink.LinkByName(ifaceName)
324: 		if err != nil {
325: 			return err
326: 		}
327: 
328: 		if err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {
329: 			return err
330: 		}
331: 
332: 		return dst.AddLinkToContainer(ctx, link, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
333: 			return nil
334: 		})
335: 	})
336: }

267: func (c *CLab) checkApplyTopologyDefinition(ctx context.Context) error {
268: 	params := *clablinks.NewVerifyLinkParams()
269: 	if len(c.Endpoints) > 0 {
270: 		runtime := c.globalRuntime()
271: 		if runtime == nil {
272: 			return fmt.Errorf("container runtime is not initialized")
273: 		}
274: 		config := runtime.Config()
275: 		if config.VerifyLinkParams != nil {
276: 			params = *config.VerifyLinkParams
277: 		}
278: 	}
279: 	params.AllowExistingEndpoint = true
280: 	if err := c.verifyLinks(ctx, &params); err != nil {
281: 		return err
282: 	}
283: 
284: 	if err := c.verifyRootNetNSLinks(); err != nil {
285: 		return err
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
289: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].CheckDeploymentConditions(ctx); err != nil {
290: 			return err
291: 		}
292: 	}
293: 
294: 	if err := c.verifyDuplicateAddresses(); err != nil {
295: 		return err
296: 	}
297: 
298: 	return c.verifyTailscaleProxy()
299: }

301: func (c *CLab) prepareApply(
302: 	ctx context.Context,
303: 	addedNodes []string,
304: 	skipLabDirFileACLs bool,
305: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
306: ) error {
307: 	existing := c.collectExistingManagementAddresses(currentNodes)
308: 	if err := c.prepareLabManagementNetwork(ctx, existing...); err != nil {
309: 		return err
310: 	}
311: 
312: 	if err := c.prepareDeployArtifacts(ctx, skipLabDirFileACLs); err != nil {
313: 		return err
314: 	}
315: 
316: 	for _, nodeName := range addedNodes {
317: 		if err := c.Nodes[nodeName].PullImage(ctx); err != nil {
318: 			return err
319: 		}
320: 	}
321: 
322: 	return nil
323: }

325: func (*CLab) removeApplyLinkEndpoints(ctx context.Context, links []clablinks.Link) error {
326: 	for _, link := range links {
327: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
328: 			if err := clablinks.RemoveOwnedInterface(
329: 				ctx,
330: 				ep.GetNode(),
331: 				ep.GetIfaceName(),
332: 			); err != nil {
333: 				return err
334: 			}
335: 		}
336: 	}
337: 
338: 	return nil
339: }

341: // try to preserve the existing addressing instead of reallocation.
342: func (c *CLab) collectExistingManagementAddresses(
343: 	currentNodes map[string]*runtimeNodeGroup,
344: ) []clabtypes.ExistingAddress {
345: 	var existing []clabtypes.ExistingAddress
346: 	for name, group := range currentNodes {
347: 		for _, ctr := range group.containers {
348: 			if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(ctr.NetworkName).Network != ctr.NetworkName {
349: 				continue
350: 			}
351: 			for _, value := range []string{ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv4addr, ctr.NetworkSettings.IPv6addr} {
352: 				if ip, err := netip.ParseAddr(value); err == nil {
353: 					existing = append(
354: 						existing,
355: 						clabtypes.ExistingAddress{NodeName: name, ContainerID: ctr.ID, Address: ip},
356: 					)
357: 				}
358: 			}
359: 		}
360: 	}
361: 	return existing
362: }

29: 	var errs []error

31:

50:

59: 	node := endpoint.GetNode()

62: 		nodeNS, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()

25: func (c *CLab) deployWithLabRuntime(
26: 	ctx context.Context,
27: 	options *DeployOptions,
28: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
29: 	if len(c.nodeFilter) != 0 {
30: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("node-filter is not supported for lab runtime %q",
31: 			c.globalRuntimeName)
32: 	}
33: 
34: 	if len(c.renderedTopology) == 0 {
35: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("rendered topology is empty")
36: 	}
37: 
38: 	if c.Config.Topology != nil &&
39: 		slices.ContainsFunc(c.Config.Topology.Links, (*clablinks.LinkDefinition).DeclaresNetem) {
40: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("link impairments (netem) are not supported for lab runtime %q",
41: 			c.globalRuntimeName)
42: 	}
43: 
44: 	if options != nil && options.reconfigure {
45: 		// --reconfigure regenerates the lab from scratch, like removing a local lab
46: 		// directory, so it also deletes the persistent node storage.
47: 		err := c.LabRuntime.Destroy(ctx, clablabruntime.DestroyRequest{
48: 			Identity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,
49: 			Name:       c.Config.Name,
50: 			Wait:       true,
51: 			Timeout:    c.timeout,
52: 			MaxWorkers: options.maxWorkers,
53: 			Cleanup:    true,
54: 		})
55: 		if err != nil {
56: 			return nil, err
57: 		}
58: 	}
59: 
60: 	req, err := c.labRuntimeDeployRequest()
61: 	if err != nil {
62: 		return nil, err
63: 	}
64: 	req.Wait = true
65: 	applyLabRuntimeDeployOptions(&req, options)
66: 
67: 	state, err := c.LabRuntime.Deploy(ctx, req)
68: 	if err != nil {
69: 		return nil, err
70: 	}
71: 
72: 	return c.containersFromLabState(state), nil
73: }

77: 		return clablabruntime.DeployRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")

80: 		return clablabruntime.DeployRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("rendered topology is empty")

185: func (l *LinkVEth) deployAEnd(ctx context.Context, idx int) error {
186: 	ep := l.Endpoints[idx]
187: 	// the peer Endpoint is the other of the two endpoints in the
188: 	// Endpoints slice. So do a +1 on the index and modulo operation
189: 	// to take care of the wrap around.
190: 	peerIdx := (idx + 1) % 2
191: 	peerEp := l.Endpoints[peerIdx]
192: 
193: 	log.Debugf("Creating Endpoint: %s ( --> %s )", ep, peerEp)
194: 
195: 	// build the netlink.Veth struct for the link provisioning
196: 	linkA := &netlink.Veth{
197: 		LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{
198: 			Name: ep.GetRandIfaceName(),
199: 			MTU:  l.MTU,
200: 			// Mac address is set later on
201: 		},
202: 		PeerName: peerEp.GetRandIfaceName(),
203: 		// PeerMac address is set later on
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	// add the link
207: 	err := netlink.LinkAdd(linkA)
208: 	if err != nil {
209: 		return err
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	// cleanup is a helper that removes the veth pair if a subsequent step fails
213: 	// after LinkAdd succeeded, preventing orphaned interfaces from blocking retries.
214: 	cleanup := func(err error) error {
215: 		if delErr := netlink.LinkDel(linkA); delErr != nil {
216: 			log.Debugf(
217: 				"failed to cleanup veth pair %s after error: %v",
218: 				ep.GetRandIfaceName(),
219: 				delErr,
220: 			)
221: 		}
222: 		return err
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	// disable TXOffloading
226: 	if err := clabutils.EthtoolTXOff(ep.GetRandIfaceName()); err != nil {
227: 		return cleanup(err)
228: 	}
229: 
230: 	// the link needs to be moved to the relevant network namespace
231: 	// and enabled (up). This is done via linkSetupFunc.
232: 	// based on the endpoint type the link setup function is different.
233: 	// linkSetupFunc is executed in a netns of a node.
234: 	// if the node is a regular namespace node
235: 	// add link to node, rename, set mac and Up
236: 	err = ep.GetNode().AddLinkToContainer(ctx, linkA,
237: 		SetNameMACAndUpInterface(linkA, ep))
238: 	if err != nil {
239: 		return cleanup(err)
240: 	}
241: 
242: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed
243: 
244: 	// e.g. host endpoints are nodeless, and therefore the B end of the veth link should
245: 	// be deployed right after the A end is deployed.
246: 	if peerEp.IsNodeless() {
247: 		return l.deployBEnd(ctx, peerIdx)
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	return nil
251: }
252: 
253: func (l *LinkVEth) deployBEnd(ctx context.Context, idx int) error {
254: 	ep := l.Endpoints[idx]
255: 	peerEp := l.Endpoints[(idx+1)%2]
256: 
257: 	log.Debugf("Assigning Endpoint: %s ( --> %s )", ep, peerEp)
258: 
259: 	// retrieve the netlink.Link for the provided Endpoint
260: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByName(ep.GetRandIfaceName())
261: 	if err != nil {
262: 		return err
263: 	}
264: 
265: 	// disable TXOffloading
266: 	if err := clabutils.EthtoolTXOff(ep.GetRandIfaceName()); err != nil {
267: 		return err
268: 	}
269: 
270: 	// Host endpoints already live in the current namespace; set them up in place.
271: 	// Other nodeless endpoints, such as the management bridge, still need their
272: 	// node-specific setup.
273: 	if ep.IsNodeless() && ep.GetNode().GetLinkEndpointType() == LinkEndpointTypeHost {
274: 		if err := SetNameMACAndUpInterface(link, ep)(nil); err != nil {
275: 			return err
276: 		}
277: 	} else if err = ep.GetNode().AddLinkToContainer(ctx, link,
278: 		SetNameMACAndUpInterface(link, ep)); err != nil {
279: 		return err
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed
283: 
284: 	if len(l.Endpoints) == 2 {
285: 		log.Infof("Created link: %s ▪┄┄▪ %s", l.Endpoints[0], l.Endpoints[1])
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	return nil
289: }

291: // getEndpointIndex returns the index of the ep endpoint belonging to l link.
292: // An error is returned when the ep is not part of the l's endpoints.
293: func (l *LinkVEth) getEndpointIndex(ep Endpoint) (int, error) {
294: 	for idx, e := range l.Endpoints {
295: 		if e == ep {
296: 			return idx, nil
297: 		}
298: 	}
299: 
300: 	// if the endpoint is not part of the link
301: 	// build a string list of endpoints and return a meaningful error
302: 	var epStrings []string
303: 	for _, e := range l.Endpoints {
304: 		epStrings = append(epStrings, e.String())
305: 	}
306: 
307: 	return -1, fmt.Errorf(
308: 		"endpoint %s does not belong to link [ %s ]",
309: 		ep.String(),
310: 		strings.Join(epStrings, ", "),
311: 	)
312: }
313: 
314: // Deploy deploys the veth link by creating the A and B sides of the veth pair independently
315: // based on the calling endpoint.
316: func (l *LinkVEth) Deploy(ctx context.Context, ep Endpoint) error {
317: 	// since each node calls deploy on its links, we need to make sure that we only deploy
318: 	// the link once, even if multiple nodes call deploy on the same link.
319: 	l.deployMutex.Lock()
320: 	defer l.deployMutex.Unlock()
321: 
322: 	// first we need to check that the provided ep is part of this link
323: 	idx, err := l.getEndpointIndex(ep)
324: 	if err != nil {
325: 		return err
326: 	}
327: 
328: 	// Retry transient netlink errors that can occur during concurrent link operations.
329: 	// deployAEnd cleans up partial state on failure, making each retry idempotent.
330: 	return retryTransientNetlink(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("deploy link %s", ep), func() error {
331: 		switch l.DeploymentState {
332: 		case LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed:
333: 			return l.deployBEnd(ctx, idx)
334: 		case LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed:
335: 			return nil
336: 		default:
337: 			return l.deployAEnd(ctx, idx)
338: 		}
339: 	})
340: }
341: 
342: func (*LinkVEth) PostDeploy(context.Context) error {
343: 	return nil
344: }
345: 
346: func (l *LinkVEth) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
347: 	l.deployMutex.Lock()
348: 	defer l.deployMutex.Unlock()
349: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateRemoved {
350: 		return nil
351: 	}
352: 	for _, ep := range l.GetEndpoints() {
353: 		err := ep.Remove(ctx)
354: 		if err != nil {
355: 			log.Debug(err)
356: 		}
357: 	}
358: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateRemoved
359: 	return nil
360: }

364: }

105: 	l.lifecycleMutex.Lock()
106: 	defer l.lifecycleMutex.Unlock()
107: 
108: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {

110: 	}
111:

113: 	switch ep {
114: 	case l.segA.Endpoints[0]:

116: 	case l.segB.Endpoints[0]:
117: 		err = l.segB.Deploy(ctx, ep)
118: 	default:
119: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %s does not belong to link [ %s, %s ]",
120: 			ep, l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.segB.Endpoints[0])
121: 	}
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return err
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed
127: 
128: 	if l.segA.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed &&
129: 		l.segB.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
130: 		return l.stitchSegments(ctx)
131: 	}
132: 
133: 	return nil
134: }

139: 	l.lifecycleMutex.Lock()
140: 	defer l.lifecycleMutex.Unlock()
141:

148: 	}

151: }

153: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) stitchSegments(ctx context.Context) error {
154: 	steps := []func() error{
155: 		func() error { return markFarEnd(l.epB, l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.labName) },
156: 		func() error { return markFarEnd(l.epA, l.segB.Endpoints[0], l.labName) },
157: 		func() error { return stitch(l.epA, l.epB) },
158: 		func() error { return stitch(l.epB, l.epA) },

174:

180: 
181: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateRemoved
182:

186: // buildVEthStitchSegment builds one veth segment: the real node endpoint plus a
187: // root-namespace far end named with a hash.
188: func buildVEthStitchSegment(
189: 	params *ResolveParams,
190: 	owner *LinkVEthStitched,
191: 	nodeEpRaw *EndpointRaw,
192: 	mtu int,
193: ) (*LinkVEth, Endpoint, error) {
194: 	seg := NewLinkVEth()
195: 	seg.MTU = mtu
196: 
197: 	nodeEp, err := nodeEpRaw.Resolve(params, owner)
198: 	if err != nil {
199: 		return nil, nil, err
200: 	}
201: 
202: 	// the far end sits in the root namespace (host node) with a short hash name
203: 	// that fits the 15 char name limit.
204: 	farName := stitchFarEndName(params.LabName, nodeEpRaw.Node, nodeEpRaw.Iface)
205: 	farGeneric := NewEndpointGeneric(GetHostLinkNode(), farName, seg)
206: 	farGeneric.MAC = nodeEp.GetMac()
207: 	farEp := NewEndpointHost(farGeneric)
208: 	seg.Endpoints = []Endpoint{nodeEp, farEp}
209: 
210: 	return seg, farEp, nil
211: }

213: func stitchFarEndName(labName, node, iface string) string {
214: 	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(labName + "\x00" + node + "\x00" + iface))
215: 	return "clab-s-" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:4]) // 7 + 8 = 15 chars
216: }

218: func markFarEnd(farEp, nodeEp Endpoint, labName string) error {
219: 	l, err := netlink.LinkByName(farEp.GetIfaceName())
220: 	if err != nil {
221: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to look up veth-stitch far end %q: %w", farEp.GetIfaceName(), err)
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	iface := nodeEp.GetIfaceAlias()
225: 	if iface == "" {
226: 		iface = nodeEp.GetIfaceName()
227: 	}
228: 
229: 	altName := StitchAltName(labName, nodeEp.GetNode().GetShortName(), iface)
230: 	if err := netlink.LinkAddAltName(l, altName); err != nil && !isAltNameNotSupportedErr(err) {
231: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to add veth-stitch altname %q: %w", altName, err)
232: 	}
233: 
234: 	return nil
235: }

237: func validateVEthStitched(r *LinkVEthStitchedRaw) error {
238: 	if len(r.Endpoints) != 2 {
239: 		return fmt.Errorf(
240: 			"veth-stitch links require exactly two endpoints, got %d",
241: 			len(r.Endpoints),
242: 		)
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	return nil
246: }

249: 	ctx context.Context,
250: 	labName string,
251: 	nodesFilter []string,
252: ) error {
253: 	return cleanupFilteredVethStitch(ctx, labName, nodesFilter, r.Endpoints)
254: }
255: 
256: func cleanupFilteredVethStitch(
257: 	ctx context.Context,
258: 	labName string,
259: 	nodesFilter []string,
260: 	endpoints []*EndpointRaw,
261: ) error {
262: 	for _, altName := range filteredVethStitchAltNames(labName, nodesFilter, endpoints) {
263: 		if err := RemoveOwnedInterface(ctx, GetHostLinkNode(), altName); err != nil {
264: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed cleaning up veth-stitch interface %q: %w", altName, err)
265: 		}
266: 	}
267: 
268: 	return nil
269: }
270: 
271: func filteredVethStitchAltNames(
272: 	labName string,
273: 	nodesFilter []string,
274: 	endpoints []*EndpointRaw,
275: ) []string {
276: 	names := make(map[string]struct{})
277: 	for _, ep := range endpoints {
278: 		if ep == nil || ep.Node == "" || ep.Iface == "" ||
279: 			!slices.Contains(nodesFilter, ep.Node) {
280: 			continue
281: 		}
282: 		names[StitchAltName(labName, ep.Node, ep.Iface)] = struct{}{}
283: 	}
284: 
285: 	result := make([]string, 0, len(names))
286: 	for name := range names {
287: 		result = append(result, name)
288: 	}
289: 	sort.Strings(result)
290: 
291: 	return result
292: }
293: 
294: // StitchAltName returns a unique name for veth-stitch links.
295: func StitchAltName(labName, node, iface string) string {
296: 	return "clab-stitch-" + clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(labName+"-"+node+"-"+iface)
297: }
298: 
299: // ToolsInterface returns the host-netns interface veth-stitch (and similar
300: // kinds) publish for node:iface under StitchAltName, or (nil, false) if none.
301: // Single seam for reporting/impairing the host side of the stitch.
302: func ToolsInterface(labName, node, iface string) (netlink.Link, bool) {
303: 	if labName == "" || node == "" || iface == "" {
304: 		return nil, false
305: 	}
306: 
307: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByName(StitchAltName(labName, node, iface))
308: 	if err != nil {
309: 		return nil, false
310: 	}
311: 
312: 	return link, true
313: }

So stitched links apply netem on node interfaces. But `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve` does NOT call `checkNetemOnVeth` — yet netem here IS applied on the node (veth) interface. So it works. The gap is:

(a) Brief veth link with netem on a `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoint, where the other node is SR-SIM (veth-stitch default): the `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` early-returns to veth-stitch BEFORE the host/mgmt-net netem check → the netem on the host side is silently dropped. (b) An explicit `type: veth-stitch` long-form link with `endpoints` declaring netem: accepted silently and applied on node ifaces. Docs say netem only on veth links — but a veth-stitch IS two veth segments, so applying netem on node endpoints works technically. Also `DeclaresNetem()` includes `LinkVEthStitchedRaw` (for lab runtime rejection). So behavior: netem on veth-stitch is intentional-ish. The docs though — check impairments.md wording.

(c) The host-side netem silently dropped in the stitched case (a): inconsistent error behavior. Also worth noting: `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` checks `epr.Node == "host"` — but a brief veth link `host:eth0 ↔ srl1:eth1` where srl1 is SR-SIM becomes stitched and the host check is bypassed. The netem for the host endpoint is silently ignored instead of erroring. Low frequency (SR-SIM + host link + netem on host side) → P4/P3.

12: // EndpointRaw is the raw (string) representation of an endpoint as defined in the topology file
13: // for a given link definition.
14: type EndpointRaw struct {
15: 	Node  string         `yaml:"node"`
16: 	Iface string         `yaml:"interface"`
17: 	MAC   string         `yaml:"mac,omitempty"`
18: 	IPv4  string         `yaml:"ipv4,omitempty"`
19: 	IPv6  string         `yaml:"ipv6,omitempty"`
20: 	Vars  map[string]any `yaml:"vars,omitempty"`
21: 	Netem *NetemRaw      `yaml:"netem,omitempty"`
22: }
23: 
24: // NewEndpointRaw creates a new EndpointRaw struct.
25: func NewEndpointRaw(node, nodeIf, mac string) *EndpointRaw {
26: 	return &EndpointRaw{
27: 		Node:  node,
28: 		Iface: nodeIf,
29: 		MAC:   mac,
30: 	}
31: }
32: 
33: // Resolve resolves the EndpointRaw into an Endpoint interface that is implemented
34: // by a concrete endpoint struct such as EndpointBridge, EndpointHost, EndpointVeth.
35: // The type of an endpoint is determined by the node it belongs to.
36: // Resolving a raw endpoint adds an associated Link and Node to the endpoint.
37: // It also adds the endpoint to the node.
38: func (er *EndpointRaw) Resolve(params *ResolveParams, l Link) (Endpoint, error) {
39: 	// check if the referenced node does exist
40: 	node, exists := params.Nodes[er.Node]
41: 	if !exists {
42: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to find node %s", er.Node)
43: 	}
44: 
45: 	genericEndpoint := NewEndpointGeneric(node, er.Iface, l)
46: 
47: 	if er.IPv4 != "" {
48: 		p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(er.IPv4)
49: 		if err != nil || !p.Addr().Is4() {
50: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
51: 				"invalid ipv4 address %q for %s:%s",
52: 				er.IPv4,
53: 				er.Node,
54: 				er.Iface,
55: 			)
56: 		}
57: 		genericEndpoint.IPv4 = p
58: 	}
59: 
60: 	if er.IPv6 != "" {
61: 		p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(er.IPv6)
62: 		if err != nil || !p.Addr().Is6() {
63: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
64: 				"invalid ipv6 address %q for %s:%s",
65: 				er.IPv6,
66: 				er.Node,
67: 				er.Iface,
68: 			)
69: 		}
70: 		genericEndpoint.IPv6 = p
71: 	}
72: 
73: 	netem, err := er.Netem.Resolve()
74: 	if err != nil {
75: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid netem for %s:%s: %w", er.Node, er.Iface, err)
76: 	}
77: 	genericEndpoint.Netem = netem
78: 
79: 	// Normalize vars to ensure JSON serialization compatibility
80: 	// (converts map[interface{}]interface{} to map[string]any)
81: 	genericEndpoint.Vars = normalizeVars(er.Vars)
82: 
83: 	if er.MAC == "" {
84: 		// if mac is not present generate one
85: 		genericEndpoint.MAC, err = clabutils.GenMac(clabconstants.ClabOUI)
86: 		if err != nil {
87: 			return nil, err
88: 		}
89: 	} else {
90: 		// if MAC is present, set it
91: 		m, err := net.ParseMAC(er.MAC)
92: 		if err != nil {
93: 			return nil, err
94: 		}
95: 		genericEndpoint.MAC = m
96: 	}
97: 
98: 	var e Endpoint
99: 
100: 	switch node.GetLinkEndpointType() {
101: 	case LinkEndpointTypeBridge, LinkEndpointTypeBridgeNS:
102: 		e = NewEndpointBridge(genericEndpoint, false)
103: 
104: 	case LinkEndpointTypeHost:
105: 		e = NewEndpointHost(genericEndpoint)
106: 
107: 	case LinkEndpointTypeVeth:
108: 		e = NewEndpointVeth(genericEndpoint)
109: 	}
110: 	if l.GetType() == LinkTypeDummy {
111: 		e = NewEndpointDummy(genericEndpoint)
112: 	}
113: 	// also add the endpoint to the node
114: 	err = node.AddEndpoint(e)
115: 	if err != nil {
116: 		return nil, err
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	return e, nil
120: }

Reasoning
Confirmed: `core/clab.go:886-901` adds virtual host and mgmt-bridge nodes to resolve nodes ("host": GetHostLinkNode()). So `params.Nodes["host"]` exists. Therefore:

- Brief veth with netem on `host:` endpoint + SR-SIM node → converted to veth-stitch, host endpoint resolved via `EndpointRaw.Resolve` → host endpoint with netem set on its `genericEndpoint`... wait, then it's added to seg as nodeEp (seg.Endpoints = [nodeEp, farEp] where nodeEp IS the host endpoint with netem). Then `applyLinkImpairments` iterates `linksEndpoints(c.Links)` → `link.GetEndpoints()` for LinkVEthStitched returns [segA.Endpoints[0], segB.Endpoints[0]] — the host endpoint IS segA.Endpoints[0] if it's the first raw endpoint! So the netem would be APPLIED to the host interface (eth0 in root ns) via the hostLinkNode's ExecFunction (root ns). Hmm — so not silently dropped, but silently applied in the root namespace to the host interface — while for a NON-stitched veth, netem on a host endpoint is an ERROR. So the same topology either errors or silently applies impairments to the host interface depending on the other endpoint's node kind. That's an inconsistency. And the mgmt-net case: `getMgmtBrLinkNode` — the mgmt-br pseudo node — would netem on mgmt-br endpoint be applied in root ns? The mgmt bridge interface is a real bridge in root ns (created by docker/podman or containerlab) — applying netem qdisc to the mgmt bridge interface in root ns is also possible.

Wait, but actually — the check at link_veth.go:71 runs for the stitched early return? No: the early return at line 58 happens BEFORE the loop. So for stitched conversion, no host/mgmt-net netem check at all. And `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve` (long form `type: veth-stitch`) has NO netem checks — so `type: veth-stitch` with `endpoints: ["host:eth0", "node1:eth1"]` and netem on the host endpoint: buildVEthStitchSegment resolves host endpoint via EndpointRaw.Resolve → LinkEndpointTypeHost → NewEndpointHost(genericEndpoint WITH netem). seg.Endpoints[0] = that host endpoint. applyLinkImpairments applies netem to host interface in root ns. Hmm.

And with SR-SIM: "clabernetes" — no, local.

So the inconsistency: host/mgmt-net netem is rejected for plain veth but silently applied for veth-stitch. Also netem on bridge endpoints (LinkEndpointTypeBridge) accepted — e.g., regular veth between two containers where one is `kind: bridge`? A topology bridge node's endpoints — LinkEndpointTypeBridge — netem set on bridge port → applied in the bridge container's netns. Does the docs mention this? Also — does `kind: bridge` node support ExecFunction? It's a container with its own netns — yes.

Hmm wait, but actually, is netem application to bridge-port interfaces even sensible? A netem qdisc on a bridge port: for egress (frames leaving the bridge through that port) it works. So netem on the bridge-side endpoint of a veth link adds delay to frames egressing the bridge. Fine.

7: 
8: # Link Impairments
9: 
10: Labs are meant to be a reflection of real-world scenarios. To make simulated networks exhibit real-life behavior you can set link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node. Link impairment feature is powered by the `tools netem` command collection:
11: 
12: * [`tools netem set`](../cmd/tools/netem/set.md)
13: * [`tools netem show`](../cmd/tools/netem/show.md)
14: * [`tools netem reset`](../cmd/tools/netem/reset.md)
15: 
16: These commands allow users to set, show and reset link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node and create labs simulating real-world network conditions.
17: 
18: ```bash title="setting packet loss at 10% rate on eth1 interface of clab-netem-r1 node"
19: containerlab tools netem set -n clab-netem-r1 -i eth1 --loss 10
20: ```
21: 
22: ## Impairments in the topology
23: 
24: Impairments can also be part of the topology, so they are set whenever the lab is deployed. The `netem` key of a link endpoint takes the same impairments as `tools netem set`, which apply to the packets the endpoint's interface sends:
25: 
26: ```yaml
27: topology:
28:   links:
29:     - type: veth
30:       endpoints:
31:         - node: r1
32:           interface: eth1
33:           netem:
34:             delay: 50ms
35:             jitter: 5ms
36:             loss: 0.5
37:         - node: r2
38:           interface: eth1
39:           netem:
40:             rate: 10000
41: ```
42: 
43: | Key          | Meaning                                                               |
44: | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
45: | `delay`      | Time to delay the packets, e.g. `100ms`                               |
46: | `jitter`     | Delay variation, e.g. `10ms`; needs a `delay`, at most `2.147483647s` |
47: | `loss`       | Random packet loss in percent                                         |
48: | `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s                                                  |
49: | `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent                                   |
50: 
51: Brief links take a list with the impairment of each endpoint, in the order of the endpoints. An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired:
52: 
53: ```yaml
54: topology:
55:   links:
56:     - endpoints: ["r1:eth1", "r2:eth1"]
57:       netem:
58:         - delay: 50ms
59:         - {}
60: ```
61: 
62: Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of veth links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. Lab runtimes such as [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) don't apply them yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails.
63: 
64: Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and when the lab is reconciled with a changed topology. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.

(End of file - total 64 lines)
</content>

Reasoning
`start.go` and `restart.go` apply impairments per node via `n.GetEndpoints()`. Note: for a veth-stitch link, `GetEndpoints()` (of the LINK) returns segment node endpoints, and each node's `GetEndpoints()` (node-level) — the node tracks its endpoints; the segment node endpoint belongs to the node. Good.

But wait — `StartNodes`: when a node starts, its interfaces are restored. For a veth link, restoring the node's interface reattaches the veth. The peer side is unchanged. Netem re-applied on the node's endpoints. Good.

Now check restart.go briefly.

Also there's a subtle issue in deploy.go: `applyLinkImpairments(ctx, linksEndpoints(c.Links))` is called AFTER linkPostDeployWorkers.Wait() — the stitch (PostDeploy) happens before impairments. But for veth-stitch: Deploy of segment ends happens during node deploy; PostDeploy stitches. If impairments were applied BEFORE PostDeploy (e.g., inside node deploy), moving interfaces into namespaces would... they apply after. OK good.

But: for `LinkVEthStitched`, `link.PostDeploy(ctx)` → stitchSegments → tc mirred redirect rules on the ROOT-NS far ends (epA/epB). The impairment on the node interface (in the node's ns) is applied after — fine.

BUT WAIT — a potential ordering issue: for stitched links, applying netem on the NODE interface (e.g., srl1:eth1) happens after stitch. The tc stitch uses `mirred` redirect on the far ends. The netem on the node iface is independent. Fine.

Now: **Does applyLinkImpairments run concurrently with anything?** In deploy it's sequential after all workers. In apply, sequential. OK.

**Concurrency**: `node.ExecFunction` for root-ns-based nodes (hostLinkNode / mgmt-br) — concurrent qdisc modifications on the same interface could conflict, but each endpoint is distinct. OK.

Now — a critical check: in `applyEndpointImpairment`, `net.InterfaceByName(endpoint.GetIfaceName())` runs inside `ExecFunction` — for the hostLinkNode (root ns based), ExecFunction uses `ns.GetCurrentNS().Path()`... fine.

For mgmt-br pseudo node (BridgeNS) — GenericLinkNode. Let me verify GenericLinkNode has ExecFunction and what it does. Also whether netem on the mgmt bridge endpoint (BridgeNS) would be applied — can it happen? Only if an EndpointRaw resolves to BridgeNS — that requires params.Nodes containing the mgmt-br node with the endpoint node name matching. What is the mgmt-br node's name in resolve nodes? `clab.go:886-901` — "add the virtual host and mgmt-bridge nodes to the resolve nodes". The key for the mgmt bridge is likely "mgmt-br" or the network name? For a veth link with endpoint "mgmt-br:something"? Not something users write. Skip.

Next steps:
1. Read core/restart.go.
2. Read cmd/deploy.go apply alias context + checkLabRuntimeCommandSupport (whether `apply`/`deploy` with lab runtime blocks netem at CLI level — deployWithLabRuntime already errors; but note: for the LAB runtime path in `c.deploy`, the netem error triggers only on `deployWithLabRuntime` — that's when initialDeploy. In `c.apply` (core/apply.go), there's NO LabRuntime branch at all — so `apply` (deploy alias) with lab runtime after initial deploy → `c.apply` runs the LOCAL reconcile path against a lab-runtime-managed lab? Reasoning
Interesting: `CLab.deploy` (line 184) routes to `deployWithLabRuntime` when LabRuntime != nil. BUT: for a lab runtime lab that is ALREADY deployed, `CLab.Deploy` → initialDeploy=false → `checkReconcileDeployOptions` → then `c.apply(...)` — the LOCAL reconcile path — even when c.LabRuntime != nil! So running `deploy` twice on a lab-runtime lab: second call goes through local `c.apply` — which uses local `runtimeNodeGroups`. Hmm wait — but `currentNodes` came from `c.runtimeNodeGroups(ctx)` at line 90 — with LabRuntime set, is that empty or does it read lab runtime state? Earlier analysis: `runtimeNodeGroups` reads local Runtimes list (local only). With LabRuntime set, local runtimes find nothing → currentNodes empty → needsInitialDeploy true → deploy route. So a lab-runtime lab NEVER reaches the local reconcile path through Deploy (needsInitialDeploy always true since local runtime sees nothing). Unless needsInitialDeploy errors differently. Fine.

But `CLab.Apply` (public, only used in tests): for a lab-runtime lab... Apply is only invoked from tests. And via CLI, apply is alias of deploy → Deploy. So applyLinkImpairments can't run against lab-runtime. OK.

Now the important remaining question set:

1. Does `c.deploy` (local) apply impairments only after ALL links deployed (line 270)? Yes — after linkPostDeployWorkers.Wait(). And for nodes started individually (start/restart), applied after each node's Start. But WAIT: there's an issue — `StartNodes`/`RestartNodes` apply impairments via `n.GetEndpoints()` — that returns the endpoints REGISTERED on the node object. In apply flow, when links are resolved (ResolveLinks), endpoints are attached to nodes. But for a node whose links were already deployed, and the node is restarted — endpoints are restored (parked interfaces). But does the netem qdisc survive `Start`? Interfaces are re-moved into the node's netns (parked → restored). Moving an interface into another netns RESETS its qdiscs — hence the comment in link_netem.go: "Impairments don't survive moving an interface to another namespace, so they have to be set again whenever the interfaces of a node are restored." Good.

2. Now check the interplay in apply: after `deployApplyNodes` (new/recreated nodes deployed) — `deployLinks` for addedLinks, then `applyLinkImpairments(ctx, linksEndpoints(c.Links))` at line 246. For a RECREATED node: its veth endpoints are recreated; the OTHER node of the link keeps its interface — but the netem qdisc on the OTHER endpoint's interface is preserved (not touched). Since the qdisc on the kept side persists, no reapply needed. And the new side gets impairments in applyLinkImpairments. But — `applyLinkImpairments(ctx, linksEndpoints(c.Links))` applies to ALL endpoints in c.Links with netem — including ones whose qdisc is already set (ReplaceImpairments = idempotent replace). Fine.

3. What about `RestartNodes` for a node with veth links where the PEER interface (kept side) has netem — fine, no changes.

4. Now — does `StartNodes` handle the veth-stitch case? When a stitched node restarts: its parked interface restored; the segment veth: node side restored; the far end (root-ns, "clab-s-xxx") — during node stop, the node side moved out (parked), the far end remains. Netem re-applied to node iface. OK.

5. Now the labruntime_gaps_test.go — read it. And core/apply_test.go exists (referenced). Let me read labruntime_gaps_test.go fully and check cmd/deploy.go apply alias and root.go support check.

6. Also need: links/netem.go beginning (lines 1-55) re-read for NetemRaw/Netem structs and validation details (I have the gist).

7. Schema check. And docs topo-def-file.md. And tests files. And diff.txt full read.

8. Also check `checkNetemOnVeth` naming oddity: it's used in dummy/macvlan/mgmt-net/host Resolve — the message says "netem is only supported on veth links, not on %s links" — but for veth links with host/mgmt-net endpoints, link_veth.go has its own check with a different message. Fine.

9. One more potential issue: `LinkVEthRaw.ToLinkBriefRaw` — appends netem list to brief even when only ONE endpoint has netem → produces [netemA, null] or [null, netemB] — schema allows null entries. But ToLinkBriefRaw is also used for... rendering export? If a nil is marshaled to YAML as `null` in the netem list — is that valid for the schema? Schema netem array items: object-or-null (confirmed earlier). OK.

10. Another check: brief link netem with MORE entries than 2 endpoints — schema maxItems 2. Good.

11. What about netem entries when the brief link has a special type (macvlan etc.)? Pre-check errors. Good.

12. What about `linkVEthRawFromLinkBriefRaw` with TWO endpoints where netem list has 2 entries → both assigned. Where list has 1 → only endpoints[0] gets it. Docs say "An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired" — consistent.

Now, the sortedStringSet/applyLinkNames etc. — not changed.

45: 			wantErr: "jitter cannot be set without setting delay",

50: 		},

88: // resolveNetemLink reads a link definition and resolves it between two fake nodes.
89: func resolveNetemLink(t *testing.T, definition string) (Link, error) {
90: 	t.Helper()
91: 
92: 	var ld LinkDefinition
93: 	if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(definition), &ld); err != nil {
94: 		return nil, err
95: 	}
96: 
97: 	return ld.Link.Resolve(&ResolveParams{Nodes: map[string]Node{
98: 		"r1": newFakeNode("r1"),
99: 		"r2": newFakeNode("r2"),
100: 	}})
101: }

Reasoning
Schema observations:

1. `netem` definition: `delay` pattern `^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h))+$` — matches time.ParseDuration patterns? time.ParseDuration accepts units: "ns", "us" (also "µs", "μs"), "ms", "s", "m", "h". The schema includes `us|µs` but NOT `μs` (Greek mu). Minor: `time.ParseDuration` accepts "μs" (U+03BC) as well as "µs" (U+00B5). So schema would REJECT "10μs" while Go accepts it. Very minor (P4, unlikely). Also the pattern allows things like "1s1ms" concatenations — ParseDuration accepts concatenated. Also the pattern rejects decimals like ".5s"? Pattern requires digits before the unit: `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` — so ".5s" rejected though ParseDuration accepts it. Minor. Not worth a finding probably.

<type>file</type>
<content>
240: 
241: ```yaml
242: endpoints: ["srl:e1-1", "ceos:eth1"]
243: ```
244: 
245: will result in a creation of a p2p link between the node named `srl` and its `e1-1` interface and the node named `ceos` and its `eth1` interface. The p2p link is realized with a veth pair.
246: 
247: ##### Extended format
248: 
249: The extended link format allows a user to set every supported link parameter in a structured way. The available link parameters depend on the Link type and provided below.
250: 
251: ###### veth
252: 
253: The veth link is the most common link type used in containerlab. It creates a virtual ethernet link between two endpoints where each endpoint refers to a node in the topology.
254: 
255: ```yaml
256: links:
257:   - type: veth
258:     endpoints:
259:       - node: <NodeA-Name>                  # mandatory
260:         interface: <NodeA-Interface-Name>   # mandatory
261:         mac: <NodeA-Interface-Mac>          # optional
262:         ipv4: <NodeA-IPv4-Address>          # optional e.g. 192.168.0.1/24
263:         ipv6: <NodeA-IPv6-Address>          # optional e.g. 2001:db8::1/64
264:         netem: <NodeA-Impairment>           # optional, see link impairments
265:       - node: <NodeB-Name>                  # mandatory
266:         interface: <NodeB-Interface-Name>   # mandatory
267:         mac: <NodeB-Interface-Mac>          # optional
268:         ipv4: <NodeB-IPv4-Address>          # optional
269:         ipv6: <NodeB-IPv6-Address>          # optional
270:         netem: <NodeB-Impairment>           # optional
271:     mtu: <link-mtu>                         # optional
272:     vars: <link-variables>                  # optional (used in templating)
273:     labels: <link-labels>                   # optional (used in templating)
274: ```
275: 
276: The `netem` key sets [link impairments](impairments.md#impairments-in-the-topology) on the interface of an endpoint.
277: 
278: ###### veth-stitch
279: 
280: The veth-stitch link type transparently stitches its two endpoints by using a veth pair per node interface then each veth is joined with a transparent tc stitch to pass the traffic.
281: 
282: ```mermaid
283: graph LR
284:     A[Node A] <-->|veth| B((tc stitch))
285:     B <-->|veth| C[Node B]
286: ```
287: 
288: This is useful for nodes whose datapath interfaces cannot be captured or impaired directly (such as SR-SIM).
289: 
290: ```yaml
291: links:
292:   - type: veth-stitch
293:     endpoints:
294:       - node: r1
295:         interface: 1/1/c1/1
296:         mac: <NodeA-Interface-Mac>          # optional
297:         ipv4: <NodeA-IPv4-Address>          # optional
298:         ipv6: <NodeA-IPv6-Address>          # optional
299:       - node: r2
300:         interface: 1/1/c1/1
301:         mac: <NodeB-Interface-Mac>          # optional
302:         ipv4: <NodeB-IPv4-Address>          # optional
303:         ipv6: <NodeB-IPv6-Address>          # optional
304: ```
305: 
306: The `mac`, `ipv4`, and `ipv6` parameters configure the node-facing endpoints. The stitch itself remains transparent to the Ethernet frames passing between them.
307: 
308: ###### mgmt-net
309: 

(Showing lines 240-309 of 914. Use offset=310 to continue.)

12: func TestRuntimeEndpointsForMacVlanExcludesParent(t *testing.T) {

14: 
15: 	node := newFakeNode("n1")
16: 	host := newFakeNode("host")
17: 	link := &LinkMacVlan{
18: 		HostEndpoint: NewEndpointMacVlan(NewEndpointGeneric(host, "eth0", nil)),
19: 		NodeEndpoint: NewEndpointVeth(NewEndpointGeneric(node, "eth1", nil)),
20: 	}
21: 
22: 	endpoints := RuntimeEndpoints(link)
23: 	if len(endpoints) != 1 {
24: 		t.Fatalf("expected one runtime endpoint, got %d", len(endpoints))
25: 	}

27: 		GetShortName() +
28: 		":" + endpoints[0].GetIfaceName(); got != "n1:eth1" {
29: 		t.Fatalf("unexpected runtime endpoint %q", got)
30: 	}
31: }

137: func endpointTokens(endpoints []Endpoint) string {
138: 	tokens := make([]string, 0, len(endpoints))
139: 	for _, ep := range endpoints {
140: 		if ep == nil {
141: 			continue
142: 		}
143: 		token := endpointToken(ep)
144: 		if token == "" {
145: 			continue
146: 		}
147: 		tokens = append(tokens, token)
148: 	}
149: 	sort.Strings(tokens)
150: 	return strings.Join(tokens, ",")
151: }
152: 
153: func endpointToken(ep Endpoint) string {
154: 	if ep == nil || ep.GetNode() == nil || ep.GetIfaceName() == "" {
155: 		return ""
156: 	}
157: 	nodeName := ep.GetNode().GetShortName()
158: 	if ep.IsNodeless() && ep.GetNode().GetLinkEndpointType() == LinkEndpointTypeBridge {
159: 		nodeName = "mgmt-net"
160: 	}
161: 	return nodeName + ":" + ep.GetIfaceName()
162: }

164: func TestOwnershipAltNameForMgmtNetEndpointIsNetworkIndependent(t *testing.T) {
165: 	t.Parallel()
166: 
167: 	defaultNode := &mgmtBridgeLinkNode{GenericLinkNode: GenericLinkNode{shortname: "br-default"}}
168: 	labNode := &mgmtBridgeLinkNode{GenericLinkNode: GenericLinkNode{shortname: "br-lab"}}
169: 
170: 	want := ownershipAltNameFor(mgmtNetOwnerName, "srl1_e1-1")
171: 	for _, node := range []*mgmtBridgeLinkNode{defaultNode, labNode} {
172: 		ep := NewEndpointBridge(NewEndpointGeneric(node, "srl1_e1-1", nil), true)
173: 		if got := ownershipAltName(ep); got != want {
174: 			t.Fatalf("bridge %q: got ownership altname %q, want %q", node.shortname, got, want)
175: 		}
176: 	}
177: }

202: 			want:    false,

208: 			t.Parallel()
209:

211: 				LinkAttrs: netlink.LinkAttrs{
212: 					Name:     "srl1_e1-1",

214: 				},
215: 			}
216: 
217: 			got := isOwnedBy(link, node, ownershipName(node), "srl1_e1-1")
218: 			if got != tt.want {

220: 			}
221: 		})

- Netem package changes (netem/netem.go): base wrote tick-based `Qopt.Latency/Jitter`; head splits `SetImpairments` into public `ReplaceImpairments` (sets `ExtendedAcknowledge`, builds qdisc, applies delay/loss/rate/corruption, replaces) + `SetImpairments` (calls ReplaceImpairments, then `Qdisc().Get()` scans all qdiscs in netns for matching Ifindex). `setDelay` now sets `Latency64`/`Jitter64` (ns pointers) with `Qopt.Latency/Jitter` left 0. `setRate` sets `Rate: uint32(min(byteRate, MaxUint32))` AND `Rate64` when byteRate > MaxUint32 (base truncated to uint32 — bug fixed; note iproute2 sets either Rate OR Rate64, not both — kernel behavior with both set unverified, low risk).
- Kernel-compat concern (candidate P3, hedged): `TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64`/`TCA_NETEM_JITTER64` are recent kernel attributes (~Linux 6.4); on older kernels (e.g., 5.15) the LATENCY64 attr may be rejected or silently ignored (tc qdisc parsing is historically lenient → delay/jitter silently 0), whereas base's tick-based write path worked everywhere. Also, this makes write path consistent with the pre-existing read path: base `cmd/tools_netem.go:336-341,386-391` ALREADY read `Latency64`/`Jitter64` (so base display was inconsistent with base writes). go.mod pins `github.com/florianl/go-tc v0.4.8`; no vendor dir, so go-tc source serialization not inspectable in snapshot.
- veth-stitch netem findings (resolved open question A):
  - `NewVEthStitchedRawFromVEth` (link_veth_stitched.go:23-28) shares the same `Endpoints` slice → netem survives brief→veth→veth-stitch conversion.
  - `buildVEthStitchSegment` → `nodeEpRaw.Resolve` → netem set on node (veth) endpoint; `LinkVEthStitched.GetEndpoints()` returns `[segA.Endpoints[0], segB.Endpoints[0]]` → impairments applied to node ifaces; per-direction semantics OK (netem applies at source node's egress; far ends are host endpoints without netem).
  - FINDING (P2 candidate): brief veth with netem on a `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoint + a node with veth-stitch default (SR-SIM) bypasses the host/mgmt-net netem rejection — `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` early-returns to veth-stitch (link_veth.go:58-60) BEFORE the rejection loop (line ~71); `params.Nodes` includes the "host" pseudo-node (core/clab.go:886-901) so the host endpoint resolves with netem attached (`EndpointRaw.Resolve` sets Netem unconditionally for ALL endpoint types) → `applyLinkImpairments` silently applies a netem qdisc to the HOST machine's interface in root ns — exactly what plain veth rejects. Same silent path for explicit long-form `type: veth-stitch` links (no `checkNetemOnVeth` in `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve`).
  - Also: netem on bridge endpoints (`LinkEndpointTypeBridge`, e.g. kind: bridge containers) is silently accepted and applied to bridge port interfaces — not documented ("Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of veth links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them", docs/manual/impairments.md ~line 62).
  - `LinkVEthRaw.ToLinkBriefRaw` (link_veth.go:24-41) appends netem list (with nil entries for unimpaired endpoints) when any endpoint has netem; `linkVEthRawFromLinkBriefRaw` errors if `len(lb.Netem) > len(link.Endpoints)`; schema allows object-or-null entries; position preserved round-trip.
- Rejection rules: `checkNetemOnVeth` (links/netem.go:96-102) rejects netem on macvlan/dummy/vxlan/mgmt-net/host Resolve; brief-form pre-check in `LinkBriefRaw.ToTypeSpecificRawLink` (link_brief.go:37-40) covers MacVLan/MgmtNet/Host only (dummy/vxlan are long-form only — consistent). `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` uses string literals `"host"`/`"mgmt-net"` for the endpoint check (minor maintainability).
- `links/netem.go` validation confirmed: jitter>0 without delay rejected; `maxNetemJitter = math.MaxInt32 * time.Nanosecond` (2.147483647s); loss 0–100 NaN-safe; `maxNetemRate = MaxUint64/1000` kbit/s; `parseNetemDuration` rejects negatives; `declaresNetem` (nil-safe, ignores empty NetemRaw).
- `links/netem_test.go` `TestNetemRawResolve` covers: empty, every-impairment, non-duration delay, negative jitter, jitter-without-delay, kernel-capped jitter, loss>100, NaN loss, rate overflow, negative corruption.
- Schema: brief link `netem` array minItems 1 maxItems 2, object-or-null entries; endpoint `netem` ref `#/definitions/netem`, `additionalProperties: false`; duration pattern `^([0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(ns|us|µs|ms|s|m|h))+$`.
- Docs (impairments.md): impairments in topology applied at deploy; netem on a link endpoint applies to packets that endpoint's interface sends; removing netem from topology does NOT remove it from running lab (use `tools netem reset`).

180: +package core
181: +

193: +)
194: +
195: +func linksEndpoints(links map[int]clablinks.Link) []clablinks.Endpoint {
196: +	var endpoints []clablinks.Endpoint
197: +	for _, link := range links {
198: +		endpoints = append(endpoints, link.GetEndpoints()...)
199: +	}
200: +
201: +	return endpoints
202: +}
203: +
204: +// applyLinkImpairments sets the link impairments of the given endpoints on their interfaces.
205: +// Impairments don't survive moving an interface to another namespace, so they have to be set
206: +// again whenever the interfaces of a node are restored.
207: +func applyLinkImpairments(ctx context.Context, endpoints []clablinks.Endpoint) error {
208: +	var errs []error
209: +	moduleLoaded := false
210: +
211: +	for _, endpoint := range endpoints {
212: +		netem := endpoint.GetNetem()
213: +		if netem == nil {
214: +			continue
215: +		}
216: +
217: +		if !moduleLoaded {
218: +			loadNetemModule(ctx)
219: +			moduleLoaded = true
220: +		}
221: +
222: +		if err := applyEndpointImpairment(ctx, endpoint, netem); err != nil {
223: +			errs = append(
224: +				errs,
225: +				fmt.Errorf("failed to set the link impairment of %s: %w", endpoint, err),
226: +			)
227: +		}
228: +	}
229: +
230: +	return errors.Join(errs...)
231: +}
232: +
233: +func applyEndpointImpairment(
234: +	ctx context.Context,
235: +	endpoint clablinks.Endpoint,
236: +	netem *clablinks.Netem,
237: +) error {
238: +	node := endpoint.GetNode()
239: +
240: +	return node.ExecFunction(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
241: +		nodeNS, err := ns.GetCurrentNS()
242: +		if err != nil {
243: +			return err
244: +		}
245: +		defer nodeNS.Close()
246: +
247: +		tcnl, err := clabnetem.NewTC(int(nodeNS.Fd()))
248: +		if err != nil {
249: +			return err
250: +		}
251: +		defer func() {
252: +			if err := tcnl.Close(); err != nil {
253: +				log.Debugf("could not close rtnetlink socket: %v", err)
254: +			}
255: +		}()
256: +
257: +		link, err := net.InterfaceByName(endpoint.GetIfaceName())
258: +		if err != nil {
259: +			return err
260: +		}
261: +
262: +		if err := clabnetem.ReplaceImpairments(
263: +			tcnl,
264: +			link,
265: +			netem.Delay,
266: +			netem.Jitter,
267: +			netem.Loss,
268: +			netem.Rate,
269: +			netem.Corruption,
270: +		); err != nil {
271: +			return err
272: +		}
273: +
274: +		log.Info(
275: +			"Set link impairments",
276: +			"node", node.GetShortName(),
277: +			"interface", endpoint.GetIfaceName(),
278: +		)
279: +
280: +		return nil
281: +	})
282: +}
283: +
284: +// loadNetemModule loads the sch_netem kernel module, which some distributions don't load on
285: +// their own.
286: +func loadNetemModule(ctx context.Context) {
287: +	if err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "modprobe", "sch_netem").Run(); err != nil {
288: +		log.Debug("failed to load the sch_netem kernel module", "err", err)
289: +	}
290: +}

327: diff --git a/docs/manual/impairments.md b/docs/manual/impairments.md
328: index 4960d7b..12b02d6 100644
329: --- a/docs/manual/impairments.md
330: +++ b/docs/manual/impairments.md
331: @@ -16,5 +16,49 @@ Labs are meant to be a reflection of real-world scenarios. To make simulated net
332:  These commands allow users to set, show and reset link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node and create labs simulating real-world network conditions.
333:  
334:  ```bash title="setting packet loss at 10% rate on eth1 interface of clab-netem-r1 node"
335:  containerlab tools netem set -n clab-netem-r1 -i eth1 --loss 10
336:  ```
337: +
338: +## Impairments in the topology
339: +
340: +Impairments can also be part of the topology, so they are set whenever the lab is deployed. The `netem` key of a link endpoint takes the same impairments as `tools netem set`, which apply to the packets the endpoint's interface sends:
341: +
342: +```yaml
343: +topology:
344: +  links:
345: +    - type: veth
346: +      endpoints:
347: +        - node: r1
348: +          interface: eth1
349: +          netem:
350: +            delay: 50ms
351: +            jitter: 5ms
352: +            loss: 0.5
353: +        - node: r2
354: +          interface: eth1
355: +          netem:
356: +            rate: 10000
357: +```
358: +
359: +| Key          | Meaning                                                               |
360: +| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
361: +| `delay`      | Time to delay the packets, e.g. `100ms`                               |
362: +| `jitter`     | Delay variation, e.g. `10ms`; needs a `delay`, at most `2.147483647s` |
363: +| `loss`       | Random packet loss in percent                                         |
364: +| `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s                                                  |
365: +| `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent                                   |
366: +
367: +Brief links take a list with the impairment of each endpoint, in the order of the endpoints. An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired:
368: +
369: +```yaml
370: +topology:
371: +  links:
372: +    - endpoints: ["r1:eth1", "r2:eth1"]
373: +      netem:
374: +        - delay: 50ms
375: +        - {}
376: +```
377: +
378: +Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of veth links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. Lab runtimes such as [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) don't apply them yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails.
379: +
380: +Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and when the lab is reconciled with a changed topology. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.

To make simulated net\n332:  These commands allow users to set, show and reset link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node and create labs simulating real-world network conditions.\n333:  \n334:  ```bash title=\"setting packet loss at 10% rate on eth1 interface of clab-netem-r1 node\"\n335:  containerlab tools netem set -n clab-netem-r1 -i eth1 --loss 10\n336:  ```\n337: +\n338: +## Impairments in the topology\n339: +\n340: +Impairments can also be part of the topology, so they are set whenever the lab is deployed. The `netem` key of a link endpoint takes the same impairments as `tools netem set`, which apply to the packets the endpoint's interface sends:\n341: +\n342: +```yaml\n343: +topology:\n344: +  links:\n345: +    - type: veth\n346: +      endpoints:\n347: +        - node: r1\n348: +          interface: eth1\n349: +          netem:\n350: +            delay: 50ms\n351: +            jitter: 5ms\n352: +            loss: 0.5\n353: +        - node: r2\n354: +          interface: eth1\n355: +          netem:\n356: +            rate: 10000\n357: +```\n358: +\n359: +| Key          | Meaning                                                               |\n360: +| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n361: +| `delay`      | Time to delay the packets, e.g. `100ms`                               |\n362: +| `jitter`     | Delay variation, e.g. `10ms`; needs a `delay`, at most `2.147483647s` |\n363: +| `loss`       | Random packet loss in percent                                         |\n364: +| `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s                                                  |\n365: +| `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent                                   |\n366: +\n367: +Brief links take a list with the impairment of each endpoint, in the order of the endpoints. An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired:\n368: +\n369: +```yaml\n370: +topology:\n371: +  links:\n372: +    - endpoints: [\"r1:eth1\", \"r2:eth1\"]\n373: +      netem:\n374: +        - delay: 50ms\n375: +        - {}\n376: +```\n377: +\n378: +Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of veth links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. Lab runtimes such as [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) don't apply them yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails.\n379: +\n380: +Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and when the lab is reconciled with a changed topology. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.\n381: diff --git a/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md b/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\n382: index eccf1ab..d29cb3a 100644\n383: --- a/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\n384: +++ b/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\n385: @@ -259,20 +259,24 @@ links:\n386:        - node: <NodeA-Name>                  # mandatory\n387:          interface: <NodeA-Interface-Name>   # mandatory\n388:          mac: <NodeA-Interface-Mac>          # optional\n389:          ipv4: <NodeA-IPv4-Address>          # optional e.g. 192.168.0.1/24\n390:          ipv6: <NodeA-IPv6-Address>          # optional e.g. 2001:db8::1/64\n391: +        netem: <NodeA-Impairment>           # optional, see link impairments\n392:        - node: <NodeB-Name>                  # mandatory\n393:          interface: <NodeB-Interface-Name>   # mandatory\n394:          mac: <NodeB-Interface-Mac>          # optional\n395:          ipv4: <NodeB-IPv4-Address>          # optional\n396:          ipv6: <NodeB-IPv6-Address>          # optional\n397: +        netem: <NodeB-Impairment>           # optional\n398:      mtu: <link-mtu>                         # optional\n399:      vars: <link-variables>                  # optional (used in templating)\n400:      labels: <link-labels>                   # optional (used in templating)\n\n(Showing lines 1-400 of 1513. To make simulated net\n These commands allow users to set, show and reset link impairments (delay, jitter, packet loss) on any link that belongs to a container node and create labs simulating real-world network conditions.\n \n ```bash title=\"setting packet loss at 10% rate on eth1 interface of clab-netem-r1 node\"\n containerlab tools netem set -n clab-netem-r1 -i eth1 --loss 10\n ```\n+\n+## Impairments in the topology\n+\n+Impairments can also be part of the topology, so they are set whenever the lab is deployed. The `netem` key of a link endpoint takes the same impairments as `tools netem set`, which apply to the packets the endpoint's interface sends:\n+\n+```yaml\n+topology:\n+  links:\n+    - type: veth\n+      endpoints:\n+        - node: r1\n+          interface: eth1\n+          netem:\n+            delay: 50ms\n+            jitter: 5ms\n+            loss: 0.5\n+        - node: r2\n+          interface: eth1\n+          netem:\n+            rate: 10000\n+```\n+\n+| Key          | Meaning                                                               |\n+| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n+| `delay`      | Time to delay the packets, e.g. `100ms`                               |\n+| `jitter`     | Delay variation, e.g. `10ms`; needs a `delay`, at most `2.147483647s` |\n+| `loss`       | Random packet loss in percent                                         |\n+| `rate`       | Rate limit in kbit/s                                                  |\n+| `corruption` | Random packet corruption in percent                                   |\n+\n+Brief links take a list with the impairment of each endpoint, in the order of the endpoints. An empty entry leaves its endpoint unimpaired:\n+\n+```yaml\n+topology:\n+  links:\n+    - endpoints: [\"r1:eth1\", \"r2:eth1\"]\n+      netem:\n+        - delay: 50ms\n+        - {}\n+```\n+\n+Impairments are supported on the node endpoints of veth links; other link types and `host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them. Lab runtimes such as [clabernetes](clabernetes/runtime.md) don't apply them yet, so deploying a topology with impairments there fails.\n+\n+Containerlab sets them again when a node is started or restarted, since a node's interfaces lose their impairments when it is stopped, and when the lab is reconciled with a changed topology. `tools netem` can still change them while the lab runs, until containerlab sets the topology's impairments again. Removing an impairment from the topology doesn't remove it from a running lab; use `tools netem reset` for that.\ndiff --git a/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md b/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\nindex eccf1ab..d29cb3a 100644\n--- a/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\n+++ b/docs/manual/topo-def-file.md\n@@ -259,20 +259,24 @@ links:\n       - node: <NodeA-Name>                  # mandatory\n         interface: <NodeA-Interface-Name>   # mandatory\n         mac: <NodeA-Interface-Mac>          # optional\n         ipv4: <NodeA-IPv4-Address>          # optional e.g. 192.168.0.1/24\n         ipv6: <NodeA-IPv6-Address>          # optional e.g. 2001:db8::1/64\n+        netem: <NodeA-Impairment>           # optional, see link impairments\n       - node: <NodeB-Name>                  # mandatory\n         interface: <NodeB-Interface-Name>   # mandatory\n         mac: <NodeB-Interface-Mac>          # optional\n         ipv4: <NodeB-IPv4-Address>          # optional\n         ipv6: <NodeB-IPv6-Address>          # optional\n+        netem: <NodeB-Impairment>           # optional\n     mtu: <link-mtu>                         # optional\n     vars: <link-variables>                  # optional (used in templating)\n     labels: <link-labels>                   # optional (used in templating)",

694: new file mode 100644
695: index 0000000..ea991e2
696: --- /dev/null
697: +++ b/links/netem.go
698: @@ -0,0 +1,126 @@
699: +package links
700: +
701: +import (
702: +	"fmt"
703: +	"math"
704: +	"slices"
705: +	"time"
706: +)
707: +
708: +// maxNetemJitter is the highest jitter the kernel accepts without capping it.
709: +const maxNetemJitter = math.MaxInt32 * time.Nanosecond
710: +
711: +// maxNetemRate is the highest rate in kbit/s that can be converted to bytes/s.
712: +const maxNetemRate = math.MaxUint64 / 1000
713: +
714: +// NetemRaw is the link impairment of an endpoint as defined in the topology file.
715: +// It applies to the packets the endpoint's interface sends.
716: +type NetemRaw struct {
717: +	Delay      string  `yaml:"delay,omitempty"`
718: +	Jitter     string  `yaml:"jitter,omitempty"`
719: +	Loss       float64 `yaml:"loss,omitempty"`
720: +	Rate       uint64  `yaml:"rate,omitempty"`
721: +	Corruption float64 `yaml:"corruption,omitempty"`
722: +}
723: +
724: +// Netem is the resolved link impairment of an endpoint.
725: +type Netem struct {
726: +	Delay      time.Duration
727: +	Jitter     time.Duration
728: +	Loss       float64
729: +	Rate       uint64
730: +	Corruption float64
731: +}
732: +
733: +// Resolve validates the impairment and returns nil if it sets nothing.
734: +func (r *NetemRaw) Resolve() (*Netem, error) {
735: +	if r == nil {
736: +		return nil, nil
737: +	}
738: +
739: +	netem := &Netem{Loss: r.Loss, Rate: r.Rate, Corruption: r.Corruption}
740: +
741: +	var err error
742: +	if netem.Delay, err = parseNetemDuration("delay", r.Delay); err != nil {
743: +		return nil, err
744: +	}
745: +	if netem.Jitter, err = parseNetemDuration("jitter", r.Jitter); err != nil {
746: +		return nil, err
747: +	}
748: +
749: +	if netem.Jitter != 0 && netem.Delay == 0 {
750: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem jitter cannot be set without setting delay")
751: +	}
752: +	if netem.Jitter > maxNetemJitter {
753: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem jitter must be at most %s", maxNetemJitter)
754: +	}
755: +	if !(netem.Loss >= 0 && netem.Loss <= 100) {
756: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem loss must be in the range between 0 and 100")
757: +	}
758: +	if !(netem.Corruption >= 0 && netem.Corruption <= 100) {
759: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem corruption must be in the range between 0 and 100")
760: +	}
761: +
762: +	if netem.Rate > maxNetemRate {
763: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netem rate must be at most %d kbit/s", uint64(maxNetemRate))
764: +	}
765: +
766: +	if *netem == (Netem{}) {
767: +		return nil, nil
768: +	}
769: +
770: +	return netem, nil
771: +}
772: +
773: +func parseNetemDuration(name, value string) (time.Duration, error) {
774: +	if value == "" {
775: +		return 0, nil
776: +	}
777: +
778: +	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(value)
779: +	if err != nil {
780: +		return 0, fmt.Errorf("netem %s %q is not a duration, e.g. 100ms: %w", name, value, err)
781: +	}
782: +	if duration < 0 {
783: +		return 0, fmt.Errorf("netem %s %q must not be negative", name, value)
784: +	}
785: +
786: +	return duration, nil
787: +}
788: +
789: +func declaresNetem(e *EndpointRaw) bool {
790: +	return e != nil && e.Netem != nil && *e.Netem != (NetemRaw{})
791: +}
792: +
793: +// checkNetemOnVeth rejects link impairments on the endpoints of a link that is not a veth link.
794: +func checkNetemOnVeth(lt LinkType, endpoints ...*EndpointRaw) error {
795: +	if slices.ContainsFunc(endpoints, declaresNetem) {
796: +		return fmt.Errorf("netem is only supported on veth links, not on %s links", lt)
797: +	}
798: +
799: +	return nil
800: +}
801: +
802: +// DeclaresNetem reports whether the link sets a link impairment on any of its endpoints.
803: +func (ld *LinkDefinition) DeclaresNetem() bool {
804: +	var endpoints []*EndpointRaw
805: +
806: +	switch l := ld.Link.(type) {
807: +	case *LinkVEthRaw:
808: +		endpoints = l.Endpoints
809: +	case *LinkVEthStitchedRaw:
810: +		endpoints = l.Endpoints
811: +	case *LinkHostRaw:
812: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{l.Endpoint}
813: +	case *LinkMacVlanRaw:
814: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{l.Endpoint}
815: +	case *LinkMgmtNetRaw:
816: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{l.Endpoint}
817: +	case *LinkDummyRaw:
818: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{l.Endpoint}
819: +	case *LinkVxlanRaw:
820: +		endpoints = []*EndpointRaw{&l.Endpoint}
821: +	}
822: +
823: +	return slices.ContainsFunc(endpoints, declaresNetem)
824: +}

1310: +func TestNetemDurationPattern(t *testing.T) {
1311: +	b, err := os.ReadFile("clab.schema.json")
1312: +	if err != nil {
1313: +		t.Fatal(err)
1314: +	}
1315: +	var schema struct {
1316: +		Definitions map[string]struct {
1317: +			Properties map[string]struct {
1318: +				Pattern string
1319: +			}
1320: +		}
1321: +	}
1322: +	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &schema); err != nil {
1323: +		t.Fatal(err)
1324: +	}
1325: +	pattern := regexp.MustCompile(schema.Definitions["netem"].Properties["delay"].Pattern)
1326: +	for _, tc := range []struct {
1327: +		duration string
1328: +		valid    bool
1329: +	}{
1330: +		{duration: "100ms", valid: true},
1331: +		{duration: "1.5s", valid: true},
1332: +		{duration: "1m30s", valid: true},
1333: +		{duration: "250µs", valid: true},
1334: +		{duration: "250us", valid: true},
1335: +		{duration: "100"},
1336: +		{duration: "-5ms"},
1337: +		{duration: "5 ms"},
1338: +	} {
1339: +		t.Run(tc.duration, func(t *testing.T) {
1340: +			if got := pattern.MatchString(tc.duration); got != tc.valid {
1341: +				t.Errorf("schema accepts = %v, want %v", got, tc.valid)
1342: +			}
1343: +			d, err := time.ParseDuration(tc.duration)
1344: +			if tc.valid && (err != nil || d < 0) {
1345: +				t.Errorf("the schema accepts %q, but the topology doesn't: %v", tc.duration, err)
1346: +			}
1347: +		})
1348: +	}
1349: +}
