1397: +*** Comments ***
1398: +This suite tests the link impairments (netem) defined in the topology: containerlab sets them when
1399: +the lab is deployed, sets them again when a node is started or restarted, and updates them on apply.
1400: +
1401: +
1402: +*** Settings ***
1403: +Library             OperatingSystem
1404: +Library             String
1405: +Resource            ../common.robot
1406: +
1407: +Suite Setup         Run Clab Command    destroy --name ${lab-name} --cleanup
1408: +Suite Teardown      Run Clab Command    destroy --name ${lab-name} --cleanup
1409: +
1410: +
1411: +*** Variables ***
1412: +${lab-name}                 link-netem
1413: +${runtime}                  docker
1414: +${topo}                     34-link-netem.clab.yml
1415: +${changed-vars}             34-link-netem.vars.changed.yml
1416: +${invalid-vars}             34-link-netem.vars.invalid.yml
1417: +${runtime-cli-exec-cmd}     docker exec
1418: +
1419: +
1420: +*** Test Cases ***
1421: +Deploy ${lab-name} lab
1422: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1423: +    ...    deploy -t ${CURDIR}/${topo}
1424: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1425: +    Should Contain    ${output}    Set link impairments
1426: +
1427: +Impairments of a brief link are set
1428: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    delay 50ms
1429: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    loss 1%
1430: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l2    eth1    rate 10Mbit
1431: +
1432: +Impairment of an extended link is set
1433: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l2    eth2    corrupt 2%
1434: +    Qdisc Should Not Contain    l1    eth2    netem
1435: +
1436: +Packets are delayed
1437: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
1438: +    ...    sudo ${runtime-cli-exec-cmd} clab-${lab-name}-l1 ping -c 3 -i 0.2 10.0.0.2
1439: +    Log    ${output}
1440: +    # a ping may be lost, so only the minimum RTT is checked
1441: +    ${min-rtt} =    Get Regexp Matches    ${output}    = ([0-9.]+)/    1
1442: +    Should Not Be Empty    ${min-rtt}
1443: +    Should Be True    ${min-rtt}[0] >= 45
1444: +
1445: +Restarted node gets its impairments again
1446: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1447: +    ...    restart -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --node l1
1448: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1449: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    delay 50ms
1450: +
1451: +Started node gets its impairments again
1452: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1453: +    ...    stop -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --node l2
1454: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1455: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1456: +    ...    start -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --node l2
1457: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1458: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l2    eth1    rate 10Mbit
1459: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l2    eth2    corrupt 2%
1460: +
1461: +Apply updates a changed impairment
1462: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1463: +    ...    apply -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --vars ${CURDIR}/${changed-vars}
1464: +    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1465: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    delay 200ms
1466: +
1467: +Apply rejects an invalid impairment
1468: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run Clab Command
1469: +    ...    apply -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --vars ${CURDIR}/${invalid-vars}
1470: +    Should Not Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
1471: +    Should Contain    ${output}    netem delay "50" is not a duration
1472: +    Qdisc Should Contain    l1    eth1    delay 200ms
1473: +
1474: +
1475: +*** Keywords ***
1476: +Run Clab Command
1477: +    [Arguments]    ${args}
1478: +    ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
1479: +    ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} ${args} 2>&1
1480: +    Log    ${output}
1481: +    RETURN    ${rc}    ${output}
1482: +
1483: +Get Qdisc

So the netlink message carries QOPT.latency=0 AND TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64=50ms. Kernel order: parse of TCA_NETEM_QOPT sets q->latency=0; then TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64 overrides with 50ms (kernel source net/sched/sch_netem.c: TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64 → q->latency = nla_get_s64). So on kernels ≥6.4 this works. On older kernels (<6.4), the LATENCY64 attribute is unknown → netlink nla policy for netem: older kernel's policy doesn't have TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64 — nla_parse for netem: attributes are parsed in a loop; unknown attributes are SKIPPED (netlink policy violations cause error only if policy says so). TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64 not in the old enum → old kernel ignores unknown attrs (nla_parse ignores attrs above maxtype). So on e.g. kernel 5.15, delay is silently dropped (link impaired only by loss/rate/corruption). Base code (tick-based QOPT.latency) worked. This IS a silent behavior regression on older kernels. 23: func NewVEthStitchedRawFromVEth(v *LinkVEthRaw) *LinkVEthStitchedRaw {
24: 	return &LinkVEthStitchedRaw{
25: 		LinkCommonParams: v.LinkCommonParams,
26: 		Endpoints:        v.Endpoints,
27: 	}
28: }
29: 
30: func (*LinkVEthStitchedRaw) GetType() LinkType {
31: 	return LinkTypeVethStitch
32: }
33: 
34: func (r *LinkVEthStitchedRaw) Resolve(params *ResolveParams) (Link, error) {
35: 	if !isInFilter(params, r.Endpoints) {
36: 		return nil, nil
37: 	}
38: 
39: 	if err := validateVEthStitched(r); err != nil {
40: 		return nil, err
41: 	}
42: 
43: 	mtu := r.MTU
44: 	if mtu == 0 {
45: 		mtu = clabconstants.DefaultLinkMTU
46: 	}
47: 
48: 	l := &LinkVEthStitched{
49: 		LinkCommonParams: r.LinkCommonParams,
50: 		labName:          params.LabName,
51: 	}
52: 	l.MTU = mtu
53: 	l.Vars = normalizeVars(l.Vars)
54: 
55: 	segA, epA, err := buildVEthStitchSegment(params, l, r.Endpoints[0], mtu)
56: 	if err != nil {
57: 		return nil, err
58: 	}
59: 
60: 	segB, epB, err := buildVEthStitchSegment(params, l, r.Endpoints[1], mtu)
61: 	if err != nil {
62: 		return nil, err
63: 	}
64: 
65: 	l.segA, l.segB = segA, segB
66: 	l.epA, l.epB = epA, epB
67: 
68: 	return l, nil
69: }
70: 
71: // LinkVEthStitched is the resolved veth-stitch link: two veth segments
72: // (nodeA<->root-ns, nodeB<->root-ns) whose root-ns ends are joined by a tc stitch.
73: type LinkVEthStitched struct {
74: 	LinkCommonParams
75: 
76: 	lifecycleMutex sync.Mutex
77: 
78: 	// since the stitch veth lives in the root ns, we need to ensure altnames
79: 	// are per-lab unique.
80: 	labName string
81: 
82: 	segA *LinkVEth
83: 	segB *LinkVEth
84: 
85: 	// the two root-ns endpoints that get stitched together
86: 	epA Endpoint
87: 	epB Endpoint
88: }
89: 
90: func (*LinkVEthStitched) GetType() LinkType {
91: 	return LinkTypeVethStitch
92: }
93: 
94: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) GetEndpoints() []Endpoint {
95: 	return []Endpoint{l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.segB.Endpoints[0]}
96: }
97: 
98: // GetRuntimeEndpoints returns every material endpoint managed by the stitched link.
99: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) GetRuntimeEndpoints() []Endpoint {
100: 	return []Endpoint{l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.segB.Endpoints[0], l.epA, l.epB}
101: }
102: 
103: // Deploy creates the veth segment belonging to ep.
104: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) Deploy(ctx context.Context, ep Endpoint) error {
105: 	l.lifecycleMutex.Lock()
106: 	defer l.lifecycleMutex.Unlock()
107: 
108: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
109: 		return nil
110: 	}
111: 
112: 	var err error
113: 	switch ep {
114: 	case l.segA.Endpoints[0]:
115: 		err = l.segA.Deploy(ctx, ep)
116: 	case l.segB.Endpoints[0]:
117: 		err = l.segB.Deploy(ctx, ep)
118: 	default:
119: 		return fmt.Errorf("endpoint %s does not belong to link [ %s, %s ]",
120: 			ep, l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.segB.Endpoints[0])
121: 	}
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return err
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateHalfDeployed
127: 
128: 	if l.segA.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed &&
129: 		l.segB.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
130: 		return l.stitchSegments(ctx)
131: 	}
132: 
133: 	return nil
134: }
135: 
136: // PostDeploy tags the two root-ns far ends and joins them with tc.
137: // if they weren't already stitched in Deploy.
138: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) PostDeploy(ctx context.Context) error {
139: 	l.lifecycleMutex.Lock()
140: 	defer l.lifecycleMutex.Unlock()
141: 
142: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
143: 		return nil
144: 	}
145: 	if l.segA.DeploymentState != LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed ||
146: 		l.segB.DeploymentState != LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed {
147: 		return fmt.Errorf("cannot stitch veth segments before both are fully deployed")
148: 	}
149: 
150: 	return l.stitchSegments(ctx)
151: }
152: 
153: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) stitchSegments(ctx context.Context) error {
154: 	steps := []func() error{
155: 		func() error { return markFarEnd(l.epB, l.segA.Endpoints[0], l.labName) },
156: 		func() error { return markFarEnd(l.epA, l.segB.Endpoints[0], l.labName) },
157: 		func() error { return stitch(l.epA, l.epB) },
158: 		func() error { return stitch(l.epB, l.epA) },
159: 	}
160: 	for _, step := range steps {
161: 		if err := retryTransientNetlink(ctx, "veth-stitch", step); err != nil {
162: 			return err
163: 		}
164: 	}
165: 
166: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateFullDeployed
167: 
168: 	return nil
169: }
170: 
171: func (l *LinkVEthStitched) Remove(ctx context.Context) error {
172: 	l.lifecycleMutex.Lock()
173: 	defer l.lifecycleMutex.Unlock()
174: 
175: 	if l.DeploymentState == LinkDeploymentStateRemoved {
176: 		return nil
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	err := errors.Join(l.segA.Remove(ctx), l.segB.Remove(ctx))
180: 
181: 	l.DeploymentState = LinkDeploymentStateRemoved
182: 
183: 	return err
184: }
185: 
186: // buildVEthStitchSegment builds one veth segment: the real node endpoint plus a
187: // root-namespace far end named with a hash.
188: func buildVEthStitchSegment(
189: 	params *ResolveParams,
190: 	owner *LinkVEthStitched,
191: 	nodeEpRaw *EndpointRaw,
192: 	mtu int,
193: ) (*LinkVEth, Endpoint, error) {
194: 	seg := NewLinkVEth()
195: 	seg.MTU = mtu
196: 
197: 	nodeEp, err := nodeEpRaw.Resolve(params, owner)
198: 	if err != nil {
199: 		return nil, nil, err
200: 	}
201: 
202: 	// the far end sits in the root namespace (host node) with a short hash name
203: 	// that fits the 15 char name limit.
204: 	farName := stitchFarEndName(params.LabName, nodeEpRaw.Node, nodeEpRaw.Iface)
205: 	farGeneric := NewEndpointGeneric(GetHostLinkNode(), farName, seg)
206: 	farGeneric.MAC = nodeEp.GetMac()
207: 	farEp := NewEndpointHost(farGeneric)
208: 	seg.Endpoints = []Endpoint{nodeEp, farEp}
209: 
210: 	return seg, farEp, nil
211: }
212: 
213: func stitchFarEndName(labName, node, iface string) string {
214: 	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(labName + "\x00" + node + "\x00" + iface))
215: 	return "clab-s-" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:4]) // 7 + 8 = 15 chars
216: }
217: 
218: func markFarEnd(farEp, nodeEp Endpoint, labName string) error {
219: 	l, err := netlink.LinkByName(farEp.GetIfaceName())
220: 	if err != nil {
221: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to look up veth-stitch far end %q: %w", farEp.GetIfaceName(), err)
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	iface := nodeEp.GetIfaceAlias()
225: 	if iface == "" {
226: 		iface = nodeEp.GetIfaceName()
227: 	}
228: 
229: 	altName := StitchAltName(labName, nodeEp.GetNode().GetShortName(), iface)
230: 	if err := netlink.LinkAddAltName(l, altName); err != nil && !isAltNameNotSupportedErr(err) {
231: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to add veth-stitch altname %q: %w", altName, err)
232: 	}
233: 
234: 	return nil
235: }
236: 
237: func validateVEthStitched(r *LinkVEthStitchedRaw) error {
238: 	if len(r.Endpoints) != 2 {
239: 		return fmt.Errorf(
240: 			"veth-stitch links require exactly two endpoints, got %d",
241: 			len(r.Endpoints),
242: 		)
243: 	}
244: 
245: 	return nil
246: }
247: 
248: func (r *LinkVEthStitchedRaw) cleanupFilteredLink(
249: 	ctx context.Context,
250: 	labName string,
251: 	nodesFilter []string,
252: ) error {
253: 	return cleanupFilteredVethStitch(ctx, labName, nodesFilter, r.Endpoints)
254: }
255: 
256: func cleanupFilteredVethStitch(
257: 	ctx context.Context,
258: 	labName string,
259: 	nodesFilter []string,
260: 	endpoints []*EndpointRaw,
261: ) error {
262: 	for _, altName := range filteredVethStitchAltNames(labName, nodesFilter, endpoints) {
263: 		if err := RemoveOwnedInterface(ctx, GetHostLinkNode(), altName); err != nil {
264: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed cleaning up veth-stitch interface %q: %w", altName, err)
265: 		}
266: 	}
267: 
268: 	return nil
269: }
270: 
271: func filteredVethStitchAltNames(
272: 	labName string,
273: 	nodesFilter []string,
274: 	endpoints []*EndpointRaw,
275: ) []string {
276: 	names := make(map[string]struct{})
277: 	for _, ep := range endpoints {
278: 		if ep == nil || ep.Node == "" || ep.Iface == "" ||
279: 			!slices.Contains(nodesFilter, ep.Node) {
280: 			continue
281: 		}
282: 		names[StitchAltName(labName, ep.Node, ep.Iface)] = struct{}{}
283: 	}
284: 
285: 	result := make([]string, 0, len(names))
286: 	for name := range names {
287: 		result = append(result, name)
288: 	}
289: 	sort.Strings(result)
290: 
291: 	return result
292: }
293: 
294: // StitchAltName returns a unique name for veth-stitch links.
295: func StitchAltName(labName, node, iface string) string {
296: 	return "clab-stitch-" + clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(labName+"-"+node+"-"+iface)
297: }
298: 
299: // ToolsInterface returns the host-netns interface veth-stitch (and similar
300: // kinds) publish for node:iface under StitchAltName, or (nil, false) if none.
301: // Single seam for reporting/impairing the host side of the stitch.
302: func ToolsInterface(labName, node, iface string) (netlink.Link, bool) {
303: 	if labName == "" || node == "" || iface == "" {
304: 		return nil, false
305: 	}
306: 
307: 	link, err := netlink.LinkByName(StitchAltName(labName, node, iface))
308: 	if err != nil {
309: 		return nil, false
310: 	}
311: 
312: 	return link, true
313: }

Also confirmed `briefDefaultLinkType(params)` — presumably checks both endpoints' node types. Let me read it to confirm it handles the host/mgmt-net pseudo-nodes (host has no default link type → probably veth; srsim → veth-stitch).

And `ToTypeSpecificRawLink` is called in `link.go:271` — during link definition parsing (unmarshal hook). So by the time c.Config.Topology.Links is populated, each LinkDefinition.Link has been converted to a specific RawLink type (LinkVEthRaw, LinkBriefRaw for unrecognized?). Let me check link.go around 250-290 to see the unmarshal path: for links with `type:` field it dispatches directly to the specific raw type; for brief links, Link = LinkBriefRaw initially, then converted? Reasoning
Confirmed the SR-SIM trigger. Everything I need is now verified. Let me finalize the findings list:

**Finding 1 (P2)**: Netem on `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoints silently applied to root-ns interfaces via the veth-stitch path.
- Location: `links/link_veth.go` L58-60 (early return before L71-73 rejection), `links/link_veth_stitched.go` L34-41/L188-211 (no netem check in `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve`/`buildVEthStitchSegment`), applied via `core/link_netem.go` L207-241 + `links/generic_link_node.go` L36-44 (ExecFunction in root ns).
- Trigger: brief link `endpoints: ["srsim:e1-1", "host:eth0"]` with netem on the host entry (SR-SIM's `DefaultLinkType()` = veth-stitch, nodes/sros/sros.go:1892), or long-form `type: veth-stitch` with a `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoint carrying netem.
- Impact: contradicts `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve`'s rejection and docs/manual/impairments.md L62 ("`host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them"); a netem qdisc is silently installed on the lab host's real interface (delay/loss/rate/corruption on host networking). On `mgmt-net` it hits the mgmt bridge port in the root ns.
- Correction: extend the endpoint rejection to `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve` (check node names in `buildVEthStitchSegment` or `validateVEthStitched`), reuse `checkNetemOnVeth`-style guard; add a regression test in `links/netem_test.go`.

**Finding 2 (P3)**: Kernel compatibility of `TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64`/`JITTER64` write path — base wrote tick-based `Qopt.Latency/Jitter`; head writes only `Latency64`/`Jitter64` (netem/netem.go L116-123). These 64-bit netlink attributes are only honored by recent kernels; on kernels that predate them the attribute is silently ignored, leaving delay/jitter at 0 (the link is only impaired by loss/rate/corruption). Base's tick-based path worked on all kernels. Suggest populating the tick-based `Qopt.Latency/Jitter` alongside (or documenting a minimum kernel version). Hedge: go-tc v0.4.8 not vendored, so exact serialization can't be inspected; smoke test covers modern GH runner kernels only.

Hmm — wait. Let me reconsider: is it possible that go-tc's NetemQopt serialization actually encodes Qopt.Latency=0 AND Latency64 — and older kernel receives TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64 as unknown attr → skipped (nla_parse ignores out-of-range attrs by default in tc policies? Actually kernel netlink attribute parsing with nla_parse: attributes with type > maxtype are simply skipped, no error). So yes silently ignored. And Qopt.latency=0 → delay 0. So on pre-LATENCY64 kernels, delay/jitter silently do nothing. When were LATENCY64 added? I believe kernel commit 7d6c6051a7cb ("sch_netem: introduce TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64")? I genuinely recall these attrs being added in 2023 (kernel 6.4-ish, together with iproute2 "tc_time_2_ticks" 64-bit support). I'll phrase it as "kernels that predate the `TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64`/`TCA_NETEM_JITTER64` attributes (added ~v6.4)" with hedging "not verifiable from the snapshot".

Actually, hmm, also important: does the kernel reject a netem qdisc whose QOPT.latency=0 but LATENCY64 set? No.

Also potential subtlety: kernel < 6.4 handling of TCA_NETEM_RATE64: RATE64 has existed for years (kernel 3.x). Fine.

**Finding 3 (P3, docs)**: `docs/manual/impairments.md` says impairments are supported on "the node endpoints of veth links" and that other link types reject them — but veth-stitch (its own link type) accepts netem on node endpoints and applies it (which is likely intended for SR-SIM netem), and this behavior is undocumented. Either update the doc to include veth-stitch or keep behavior-consistent wording. Hmm — is it really "accepted and applied"? For long-form veth-stitch: endpoint netem resolved in buildVEthStitchSegment → nodeEp (SR-SIM node) with netem → GetEndpoints returns node endpoints → applied to SR-SIM's interface in its container netns. Yes.

I could merge Finding 3 into Finding 1 (same root cause: the stitched path lacks netem handling). Root cause is the same: `LinkVEthStitchedRaw` netem semantics were not fully considered. One finding per root cause — merge: the P2 covers the silent host/mgmt-net impairment; the docs aspect (undocumented veth-stitch support) is part of the same correction. I'll fold it in.

# Review: per-endpoint link impairments (netem) in the topology

## Summary

This PR adds `netem` link impairments to topology files. Endpoints carry a `NetemRaw` → `Netem` definition, validation lives in `links/netem.go`, and `core/link_netem.go` applies a netem qdisc to each impaired endpoint's interface via `ExecFunction` at deploy, start, restart, and reconcile time. The `netem/netem.go` write path was switched from tick-based `Qopt.Latency/Jitter` to the 64-bit `Latency64/Jitter64` attributes, the lab-runtime (clabernetes) path rejects topologies that declare impairments, and docs/schema/smoke tests were updated.

The feature is well structured overall: validation is centralized, the brief-link positional list matches the schema, re-application after start/restart is handled, and the lab-runtime rejection plus the smoke suite (deploy, restart, start, apply-update, apply-reject) cover the main flows well. The review found one correctness hole in the veth-stitch path, one kernel-compatibility regression risk, and two minor consistency items.

## Severity summary

| Priority | Finding | Location |
|---|---|---|
| P2 | `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoints silently get a netem qdisc in the root namespace through the veth-stitch path | `links/link_veth_stitched.go` |
| P3 | Delay/jitter now written only via `TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64`/`JITTER64`, which older kernels silently ignore | `netem/netem.go` |
| P4 | Schema allows `netem` on all extended link types while the runtime rejects non-veth types | `schemas/clab.schema.json` |
| P4 | String literals `"host"`/`"mgmt-net"` duplicate existing constants | `links/link_veth.go` |

## Findings

### 1. (P2) Netem on `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoints is silently applied in the root namespace via the veth-stitch path

**Location:** [links/link_veth_stitched.go#L34-L69](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth_stitched.go#L34-L69) (with the introducing guard at [links/link_veth.go#L58-L60](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth.go#L58-L60) and the application path [core/link_netem.go#L207-L241](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/core/link_netem.go#L207-L241))

**Problem:** `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve` rejects netem on `host`/`mgmt-net` endpoints (`link_veth.go:71-73`), and `docs/manual/impairments.md` documents that "`host` or `mgmt-net` endpoints reject them". But `Resolve` takes an early return at `link_veth.go:58-60` when the brief link's default link type is veth-stitch, before that check runs. `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve` performs no netem check at all: `buildVEthStitchSegment` calls `nodeEpRaw.Resolve`, and `EndpointRaw.Resolve` attaches `genericEndpoint.Netem` unconditionally for every node kind (`links/endpoint_raw.go:73-77`). `LinkVEthStitched.GetEndpoints()` then returns the two node-side endpoints (`link_veth_stitched.go:94-96`), so `applyLinkImpairments` sees the host endpoint's netem and applies it via `GenericLinkNode.ExecFunction`, which runs in the root namespace (`links/generic_link_node.go:36-44`).

**Trigger:** A brief link whose endpoint is `host:` or `mgmt-net:` with a `netem` entry, combined with an SR-SIM endpoint — `sros.DefaultLinkType()` returns `LinkTypeVethStitch` (`nodes/sros/sros.go:1892-1894`), and `briefDefaultLinkType` considers both endpoints of the brief link. The same silent path also triggers with an explicit long-form `type: veth-stitch` link that has a `host:`/`mgmt-net:` endpoint carrying `netem`.

```yaml
links:
  - endpoints: ["srsim:e1-1", "host:eth0"]
    netem:
      - delay: 50ms
      - delay: 500ms   # silently applied to eth0 on the lab host itself
```

**Impact:** Containerlab installs a netem qdisc on the lab host's real interface (or on the management bridge port) in the root namespace — delay, loss, rate, or corruption degrade host networking with no error, while plain veth links error out on the same configuration. The documented rejection does not hold for these paths, and there is no unit test covering it (`links/netem_test.go` covers only plain veth).

**Correction:** Mirror the `host`/`mgmt-net` endpoint rejection in `LinkVEthStitchedRaw.Resolve` (e.g. in `buildVEthStitchSegment`, where the node name is available, reuse the `declaresNetem` check from `LinkVEthRaw.Resolve`), and add the two failing cases to `links/netem_test.go`. While there, the veth-stitch support for netem on *node* endpoints (which the SR-SIM use case implies is intended) should also be stated explicitly in `docs/manual/impairments.md` instead of the current "node endpoints of veth links" wording, which implies veth-stitch rejects them.

### 2. (P3) Delay/jitter write path now depends on `TCA_NETEM_LATENCY64`/`JITTER64`, which older kernels silently ignore

**Location:** [netem/netem.go#L115-L123](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/netem/netem.go#L115-L123)

**Problem:** The base code wrote `Qopt.Latency`/`Qopt.Jitter` as converted ticks, which the netem qdisc has honored since long ago. The head code leaves `Qopt.Latency`/`Qopt.Jitter` at zero and sets only `Netem.Latency64`/`Netem.Jitter64` (nanoseconds). These 64-bit attributes are only understood by recent kernels; on kernels that predate them the unknown attributes are silently skipped by the qdisc's attribute parser, leaving delay and jitter at 0 — the topology deploys successfully but the link is only impaired by loss/rate/corruption. The base implementation produced working impairments on all kernels, so this is a behavior regression on older hosts.

**Trigger:** Deploying a topology with `delay`/`jitter` netem on a host running a kernel without the 64-bit netem latency attributes.

**Impact:** Silent loss of the delay/jitter impairment (the most common netem use) on older kernels; users get no error and may only notice via the smoke-style `tc qdisc show` or packet measurements. Note this makes the write path *consistent* with the pre-existing read path — `cmd/tools_netem.go` already read `Latency64`/`Jitter64` in the base, so base's `netem show` output disagreed with base's writes; the PR fixes that inconsistency — but the compatibility tradeoff is not documented.

**Correction:** Prefer populating the tick-based `Qopt.Latency`/`Qopt.Jitter` alongside the 64-bit attributes (the kernel parses `TCA_NETEM_QOPT` before the override attributes, so modern kernels still honor the 64-bit values), or document a minimum kernel version for delay/jitter in `docs/manual/impairments.md`. The go-tc module (`v0.4.8`) is not vendored in the snapshot, so the exact attribute serialization order could not be verified here; the smoke test runs only on modern GitHub runner kernels and would not catch this.

### 3. (P4) Schema allows `netem` on every extended link type although the runtime rejects all but veth/veth-stitch

**Location:** [schemas/clab.schema.json#L1565-L1567](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1565-L1567)

**Problem:** The `netem` property was added to the shared `link-endpoint` definition, which all extended link types reference (`link-type-dummy`, `link-type-host`, `link-type-macvlan`, `link-type-mgmt-net`, `link-type-vxlan`, `link-type-vxlan-stitch`, `link-type-veth`, `link-type-veth-stitch`). The Go code rejects netem on all of these except veth and veth-stitch (`checkNetemOnVeth` in `links/link_dummy.go:25`, `link_host.go:57`, `link_macvlan.go:62`, `link_mgmt-net.go:42`, `link_vxlan.go:36`), so the schema accepts topologies the runtime always refuses. The runtime error is clear, so this is a schema/behavior mismatch rather than a user-facing bug.

**Trigger:** Validating any extended non-veth link with an endpoint `netem` key against `clab.schema.json`.

**Impact:** Misleading editor autocompletion/validation; users discover the rejection only at deploy time. Optional correction: scope `netem` to a veth/veth-stitch-specific endpoint definition, or accept the permissive schema and note the runtime restriction in the endpoint property description.

### 4. (P4) `link_veth.go` compares pseudo-node names against string literals instead of existing constants

**Location:** [links/link_veth.go#L70-L73](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/c904ce8caad8d546cadbef2bad16945ece5478b8/links/link_veth.go#L70-L73)

**Problem:** The new rejection uses `epr.Node == "host" || epr.Node == "mgmt-net"`, while the same strings already exist as named values: `LinkTypeHost`/`LinkTypeMgmtNet` in `links/link.go:74-76` and `mgmtNetOwnerName` in `links/link_mgmt-net.go:123`. A typo or rename of the pseudo-node names would silently break this guard.

**Trigger:** Maintenance change to the pseudo-node names or the netem guard.

**Impact:** Minor maintainability cost only; optional improvement.

**Correction:** Use `string(LinkTypeHost)`/`string(LinkTypeMgmtNet)` (or dedicated pseudo-node-name constants) in the check.

## Coverage notes

- All 28 changed paths in `manifest.json` were reviewed, including the full `diff.txt` (1,513 lines), plus relevant surrounding code: `links/link_veth_stitched.go`, `links/generic_link_node.go`, `core/apply.go`, `core/clab.go` (pseudo-node registration), `cmd/tools_netem.go`, `nodes/sros/sros.go`, and the existing `links/apply_test.go`.
- This was a source-only review: no tests, formatter, or CI runs were executed. Test quality was assessed from source; the robot suite's assertions match the implementation's error strings, but execution was not observed.
- `go-tc v0.4.8` is not vendored in the snapshot, so the netlink attribute serialization of `Latency64`/`Jitter64`/`Rate64` was inferred from the go-tc API semantics rather than confirmed against library source; the kernel version range that honors the 64-bit latency attributes is likewise not verifiable from the snapshot.
- The behavior of `apply`/`deploy` when a node's container is currently stopped (where `ExecFunction` fails and aborts the whole command) was not traced end-to-end; the pre-existing `start`/`restart` flows reduce but do not eliminate this exposure.
- Setting both `Rate` (capped to `MaxUint32`) and `Rate64` in `setRate` differs from iproute2 (which sets one or the other); on kernels lacking `TCA_NETEM_RATE64` the rate silently caps at 4 Gbit/s, which is an improvement over the base truncation but not verified against the kernel's precedence rules.
